## 2026-07-27 live Engine/ModelRunner acknowledgement wiring gate

### Objective

The dependency-light acknowledgement protocol is now wired into the real
Python `LLMEngine`/`ModelRunner` control path.

The existing ordinary call contract remains:

```python
result = model_runner.call(method_name, *args)
```

It still broadcasts fire-and-forget to workers and returns the rank-0 local
result.

The new Engine API is:

```python
local_result, worker_acks = (
    engine.call_model_runner_acknowledged(
        method_name,
        *args,
        timeout_s=...,
    )
)
```

This phase was validated without constructing CUDA ModelRunner objects,
starting NCCL, loading checkpoints, or using a remote server.

### Artifacts

- Design:
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-model-runner-live-ack-wiring-design.md`
- Plan:
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-model-runner-live-ack-wiring.md`
- Core protocol:
  `tinyvllm/engine/model_runner_command_ack.py`
- Live wiring:
  `tinyvllm/engine/model_runner.py`
  `tinyvllm/engine/llm_engine.py`
- Tests:
  `tools/test_model_runner_command_ack.py`
  `tools/test_model_runner_live_ack_wiring.py`
  `tools/test_model_runner_spec_verify.py`

### Wiring implemented

`LLMEngine.__init__` now:

- creates one unidirectional `multiprocessing.Pipe(duplex=False)` per worker;
- retains rank-indexed receive endpoints;
- passes exactly one sender to each spawned worker ModelRunner;
- closes the parent duplicate sender after `Process.start()`;
- constructs `ModelRunnerCommandAckCollector` for worker ranks `1..TP-1`.

`ModelRunner` now:

- accepts optional `ack_sender`;
- owns monotonic command IDs;
- broadcasts `ModelRunnerCommandEnvelope` through existing shared memory;
- accepts one legacy list-form command as fire-and-forget compatibility;
- runs worker commands through `execute_acknowledged_command()`;
- preserves `call()` local return and fire-and-forget behavior;
- exposes `dispatch_command(..., requires_ack=...)`.

`LLMEngine.call_model_runner_acknowledged()`:

- handles TP=1 locally with no worker acknowledgements;
- dispatches one acknowledged envelope for TP>1;
- runs the same method on rank 0;
- poisons the collector if rank-0 execution fails after dispatch;
- collects workers against process `is_alive()` liveness;
- returns only after all worker outer acknowledgements are `ok`.

Engine exit closes owned receive endpoints through a compatibility-safe
optional cleanup hook. The existing distributed exit barrier is unchanged and
remains a GPU crash-recovery limitation.



```text

tinyvllm.engine.model_runner_command_ack
```

## 2026-07-27 ModelRunner command acknowledgement CPU gate

### Objective

The next runtime prerequisite was implemented as a standard-library-only
control-plane acknowledgement protocol. It solves the specific limitation
that the existing ModelRunner worker loop discards non-rank-0 return values
and exceptions.

This phase does not modify `LLMEngine`, `ModelRunner`, scheduler admission,
CUDA, NCCL, or checkpoint execution.

### Artifacts

- Design:
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-model-runner-command-ack-channel-design.md`
- Plan:
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-model-runner-command-ack-channel.md`
- Protocol:
  `tinyvllm/engine/model_runner_command_ack.py`
- Tests:
  `tools/test_model_runner_command_ack.py`

### Protocol implemented

`ModelRunnerCommandEnvelope` binds:

```text
monotonic command id
public method name
tuple args
requires_ack flag
```

`ModelRunnerCommandAck` reports:

```text
command id
worker rank
outer status: ok | error
result
bounded error type/detail
```

`execute_acknowledged_command()` preserves fire-and-forget behavior when
`requires_ack=False`. For acknowledged commands it sends exactly one `ok`
result or one bounded ordinary-exception `error`. `BaseException` is not
converted into an acknowledgement.

`ModelRunnerCommandAckCollector`:

- owns one receive endpoint per worker rank;
- requires ranks to be contiguous from `1`;
- polls against one absolute monotonic deadline;
- orders successful acknowledgements by rank;
- detects outer worker error, missing rank timeout, dead worker, stale/future
  command ID, wrong rank, malformed values, closed pipe, poll/recv failure, and
  invalid liveness;
- poisons itself after any uncertain worker outcome and rejects reuse;
- does not conflate outer transport/execution `ok` with an inner hybrid-prefix
  restore result such as `miss`.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 hybrid-prefix restore-ticket CPU gate

### Objective and ownership boundary

The next engine-integration prerequisite was implemented as a dependency-light
two-phase restore-ticket protocol:

```text
Engine/Scheduler control plane:
  complete KV reservation
  + HybridStateSlotAllocator lease
  + request publication

ModelRunner participant:
  rank-local HybridStateTensorPool
  + rank-local snapshot cache
  + explicit prepare acknowledgement
```

The implementation deliberately does not modify `LLMEngine.step()`, scheduler
hybrid-prefix admission, or the current worker shared-memory RPC. The existing
RPC still discards non-rank-0 return values and has no cross-rank error
acknowledgement.

### Artifacts

- Design:
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-hybrid-prefix-restore-ticket-design.md`
- Plan:
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-hybrid-prefix-restore-ticket.md`
- Protocol:
  `tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_hybrid_prefix_restore_ticket.py`
- Tests:
  `tools/test_qwen35_hybrid_prefix_restore_ticket.py`

### Protocol implemented

The cross-process-safe payload binds:

```text
ticket id
request id
exact Qwen3.5 prefix key
exact token tuple
exact KV block identities
generation-checked state lease
```

Each modeled rank-local participant returns exactly one explicit
acknowledgement:

```text
prepared
miss
error
```

The coordinator state machine is:

```text
reserved -> prepared -> committed
    |           |
    +-----------+-> rolled_back
                    rollback_failed
```

Properties covered:

- reserve privately holds a complete prefix-plus-suffix KV table and central
  lease without changing `Sequence`;
- every participant activates and restores its own pool row;
- the request remains pristine until every participant acknowledges
  `prepared`;
- any participant miss/error releases earlier prepared rows, allocator lease,
  and complete KV reservation;
- precommit validates acknowledgements, allocator ownership, participant
  prepared identity, request pristine state, and complete reservation
  identity before publication;
- commit attaches the complete KV table and publishes lease metadata only
  after all participant checks pass;
- cleanup failure is never reported as successful rollback: the ticket enters
  `rollback_failed`, Engine resources are released best-effort, and the
  coordinator is poisoned so an allocator slot cannot be reused while a rank
  may retain a stale binding;
- `token_hash` remains an independent cache-key identity; only
  `terminal_block_hash` is required to match the BlockManager chain;
- payloads and acknowledgements survive pickle round trips.

## 2026-07-27 Atomic complete sequence block reservation

### Why this gate was required

The exact hybrid-prefix acquisition primitive could hold reusable prefix KV
references and restore aligned Qwen3.5 linear state, but a real request also
needs uncached suffix blocks. Existing `BlockManager.allocate()` writes
directly into `Sequence.block_table`, so a later state-restore failure could
otherwise expose or require unwinding a partial request.

This phase adds a private complete-table transaction before any scheduler
integration:

```text
exact reusable prefix refs
+ newly allocated suffix blocks
= one private complete request block table
```

Artifacts:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-atomic-sequence-block-reservation-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-atomic-sequence-block-reservation.md`;
- `tinyvllm/engine/block_manager.py`:
  `SequenceBlockReservation`, `reserve_sequence_blocks()`,
  `attach_sequence_reservation()`, and
  `release_sequence_reservation()`;
- `tools/test_chunked_prefill.py`:
  cold/warm, sampleable cap, collision, capacity, rollback, attachment,
  stale identity, malformed input, and compatibility tests.

Scheduler and ModelRunner were not modified in this phase.

### Ownership and transaction semantics

`SequenceBlockReservation` records:

```text
complete ordered block_ids
exact reusable prefix block identities
cached token count
prefix block count
new suffix block count
reserved/attached/released state
```

`reserve_sequence_blocks()`:

1. requires a pristine request;
2. defaults to the existing `max_reusable_tokens()` sampleable-token cap;
3. discovers the complete exact reusable prefix without mutation;
4. prechecks total free capacity;
5. acquires one reference per reusable prefix block;
6. allocates every suffix block privately;
7. returns without changing request metadata.

`attach_sequence_reservation()` validates counts, sampleable cap, current
block ownership, exact token chain, generation, and hash before copying the
complete table and cached/computed counters into the request.

`release_sequence_reservation()` validates reservation structure and current
ownership before releasing exactly one reference per block.

### Failure atomicity findings and fixes

The initial RED was:

```text
AttributeError:
'BlockManager' object has no attribute 'reserve_sequence_blocks'
```

The first GREEN attempt exposed a real rollback defect:

```text
generation BEFORE (1, 0, ...)
generation AFTER  (1, 1, ...)
```

Reason: `_allocate_block()` increments content generation and clears cached
metadata, while ordinary deallocation cannot restore that pre-call identity.

The final rollback snapshots only candidate suffix blocks and their affected
hash-index entries before mutation. On exception it restores:

- refcount;
- content generation;
- hash and exact tokens;
- `hash_to_block_id`;
- `hash_to_block_ids`;
- `used_block_ids`;
- exact free-list order.

Additional injected tests cover:

- second suffix allocation fails before mutation;
- second suffix allocation mutates then raises;
- two idle cached blocks share one hash and rollback must restore the complete
  collision set and primary entry.

Self-review also corrected:

- default cache cap from `len(seq)` to `max_reusable_tokens(seq)`, preventing
  a full block-aligned prompt from skipping the last sampleable token;
- malformed block IDs and identity structures now fail with `ValueError`
  before internal indexing;
- stale ownership and repeated terminal operations fail closed.

### Runtime ownership boundary discovered

The real engine split is:

```text
Scheduler:
  BlockManager + request queues + HybridStateSlotAllocator

ModelRunner:
  HybridStateTensorPool + layer adapters + actual state tensors
```

Therefore the completed CPU coordinator must not simply be installed inside
Scheduler. That would create a second state owner and would not match the
multi-process/GPU runtime.

The next gate must be an explicit Engine↔ModelRunner two-phase restore ticket:

```text
Scheduler privately reserves complete KV table + lease identity
ModelRunner prepares/validates snapshot restore without publishing request
Engine commits scheduler request metadata only after all ranks acknowledge
failure on any rank rolls back runner state preparation and KV reservation
```

The existing scheduler hybrid-prefix fail-closed check remains unchanged.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 hybrid prefix runtime acquisition transaction

### Scope and artifacts

This CPU-only phase adds the ownership transaction that was missing between
the exact hybrid prefix snapshot cache and runtime request metadata:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-hybrid-prefix-runtime-acquisition-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-hybrid-prefix-runtime-acquisition.md`;
- `tinyvllm/engine/block_manager.py`:
  content-lifetime `Block.generation`, `PrefixBlockReservation`,
  `reserve_exact_prefix()`, `attach_prefix_reservation()`, and
  `release_prefix_reservation()`;
- `tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_hybrid_prefix_acquisition.py`:
  `Qwen35HybridPrefixAcquireCoordinator`;
- `tools/test_chunked_prefill.py`:
  generation, exact reservation, multi-owner transfer, partial miss,
  activation rollback, and terminal-state tests;
- `tools/test_qwen35_hybrid_prefix_acquisition.py`:
  real block manager, allocator, tensor pool, adapters, cross-layer
  transaction, and snapshot-cache integration tests.

`Scheduler._allocate_request_storage()` remains unchanged and fail-closed:

```text
hybrid prefix reuse requires aligned state snapshot
```

No scheduler main-path wiring, ModelRunner command, GPU KV access, checkpoint,
local GPU process, or remote process was added.

### Generation and reservation semantics

`Block.generation` now describes one physical KV content lifetime:

- first assignment to new content increments `0 -> 1`;
- deallocation preserves generation because KV bytes remain reusable;
- exact idle-cache reactivation preserves generation;
- assigning that physical block to different content increments generation;
- every snapshot identity remains `(block_id, generation, block_hash)`.

`reserve_exact_prefix()` validates the complete full-block chained-token
prefix before ownership mutation. A partial chain is a read-only normal miss.
For a full hit it holds `owner_count` references on every block, including
generation-preserving activation of idle cached blocks.

Reservation state is explicit:

```text
reserved -> attached
reserved -> released
```

Double attach/release fails closed. Attachment transfers already-held
references to destination sequences without changing refcounts.

### Coordinator transaction

`Qwen35HybridPrefixAcquireCoordinator.acquire()` performs:

```text
validate destination requests and exact prompt prefix
reserve exact KV chain for all destination owners
allocate one HybridStateLease per request
activate every pool binding
restore snapshot through Qwen35HybridPrefixSnapshotCache.acquire()
attach KV reservation and lease metadata only after restore succeeds
```

Validation requires every destination prompt to contain the exact cached token
tuple at its start. This closes a self-review bug where a valid snapshot could
otherwise have been attached to an unrelated prompt.

Normal KV/snapshot misses return `False`. State exhaustion, pool activation
failure, and restore exceptions re-raise after releasing all newly acquired
pool bindings, allocator leases, and KV references. Failed attempts preserve:

```text
block_table == []
num_cached_tokens == 0
num_computed_tokens == 0
hybrid_state_slot_id == -1
hybrid_state_generation == 0
```

A successful call attaches only the exact reusable prefix. It deliberately
does not allocate the uncached suffix.

## Qwen3.5 Hybrid Prefix Snapshot Cache Primitive (2026-07-27)

### Motivation

The existing hash-based prefix cache can identify reusable full-attention KV
blocks. Qwen3.5 linear-attention layers also require convolution and recurrent
state at exactly the same prefix boundary. Reusing KV without that state would
start the suffix from an inconsistent history.

The scheduler therefore remains correctly fail-closed:

```text
hybrid prefix reuse requires aligned state snapshot
```

This phase establishes that missing snapshot primitive without wiring it into
the scheduler, ModelRunner, GPU KV cache, or a real checkpoint.

### Files

```text
tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_hybrid_prefix_cache.py
tools/test_qwen35_hybrid_prefix_cache.py
docs/superpowers/specs/
  2026-07-27-qwen35-hybrid-prefix-snapshot-cache-design.md
docs/superpowers/plans/
  2026-07-27-qwen35-hybrid-prefix-snapshot-cache.md
```

### Contract

`Qwen35HybridPrefixSnapshotCache` binds:

```text
exact prefix tokens
model/layout/TP/dtype/block-size fingerprint
full KV chain block_id/generation/hash identities
one exact row of every linear layer convolution/recurrent state
```

The state snapshot is stored once and can be broadcast into multiple
out-of-order destination request leases. All destination layers and rows are
restored through one `Qwen35CrossLayerStateTransaction.commit()`.

Publication validates and clones the complete source state before index
mutation. Acquisition validates exact tokens and current KV identities before
any state write. A malformed later-layer candidate fails before writes; a
later copy failure restores every destination layer/row.

The cache uses deterministic LRU and enforces both:

```text
current_entries <= max_entries
current_state_snapshot_bytes <= max_bytes
```

Oversize entries are rejected without partial publication. Explicit block
invalidation and lazy stale-generation invalidation remove dependent entries.

## Qwen3.5 Packed Heterogeneous Layer-Stack Gate (2026-07-27)

### Objective and scope

This CPU-only production-correctness prerequisite combines request-isolated
full-attention decoder layers and stateful linear-attention decoder layers in
one explicit packed schedule. It does not load a checkpoint, execute CUDA, or
wire embeddings, final norm, lm head, scheduler, or ModelRunner.

The implemented schedule gate is:

```text
layer 0: linear_attention
layer 1: full_attention
layer 2: linear_attention
token_counts: (2, 1, 3)
```

Implementation and focused test:

```text
tinyvllm/layers/qwen35_packed_layer_stack.py
tools/test_qwen35_packed_layer_stack.py
```

Design and execution records:

```text
docs/superpowers/specs/
  2026-07-27-qwen35-packed-heterogeneous-layer-stack-design.md
docs/superpowers/plans/
  2026-07-27-qwen35-packed-heterogeneous-layer-stack.md
```

### Transaction and isolation contract

`Qwen35PackedHeterogeneousLayerStack` validates that transaction adapter layer
indices exactly match all linear-attention tuple indices. It then:

1. validates packed leases/counts/positions/hidden metadata;
2. gathers all linear-layer state once through
   `Qwen35CrossLayerStateTransaction`;
3. executes layers in model order;
4. executes every full-attention layer as separate request segments;
5. pairs every linear request segment with the same request row from the
   matching linear layer state;
6. accumulates candidates without any intermediate state commit;
7. commits all linear-layer candidates once after the complete stack succeeds.

The focused test directly observes one transaction `gather()` and one
transaction `commit()`. It also verifies that input hidden states and position
IDs are unchanged.

## Qwen3.5 Cross-Layer Linear-State Transaction Gate (2026-07-27)

### Motivation

The packed linear decoder wrapper commits one layer at a time. Directly
building a heterogeneous model stack from that wrapper would allow this
failure:

```text
linear layer 0 state committed
full or linear layer 1 fails
model forward fails with layer 0 state still advanced
```

Added a cross-layer coordinator before constructing the model stack:

```text
tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_state_transaction.py
tools/test_qwen35_cross_layer_state_transaction.py
```

Written design and plan:

```text
docs/superpowers/specs/
2026-07-27-qwen35-cross-layer-state-transaction-design.md

docs/superpowers/plans/
2026-07-27-qwen35-cross-layer-state-transaction.md
```

### Interface and construction

```python
Qwen35CrossLayerStateTransaction(
    adapters: tuple[Qwen35LayerStateAdapter, ...],
)

gather(leases)
commit(leases, candidates)
```

Construction requires:

- a non-empty tuple;
- only `Qwen35LayerStateAdapter` entries;
- one shared `HybridStateTensorPool`;
- unique layer indices.

Adapter order defines transaction layer order.

### Transaction semantics

`gather()` returns one batched convolution/recurrent pair per adapter while
preserving adapter and lease order.

`commit()`:

1. validates the complete lease tuple through every adapter;
2. requires one candidate pair per adapter;
3. validates every candidate batch shape/dtype/device;
4. snapshots every selected row in every layer;
5. copies in layer/request/convolution-then-recurrent order;
6. directly restores all snapshotted rows if any copy fails.

Rollback does not use `_copy_component`, so an injected copy failure cannot
also block restoration.

The main fixture uses:

```text
linear layers: 1 and 3
pool slots: 0, 1, 2
selected lease order: slot 2, slot 0
```

The injected failure occurs on copy 7:

```text
layer 1: both selected request rows fully copied (4 copies)
layer 3: slot 2 fully copied (2 copies)
layer 3: slot 0 convolution copied
layer 3: slot 0 recurrent fails
```

After failure, both layers and all three slots exactly match pre-commit
snapshots.

```text
tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_state_transaction.py
```



```text

```

passed. This was an environment write-path issue, not a source failure.

### Allowed conclusion and next gate

Allowed:

> packed Qwen3.5 linear-attention layer-state batches.

Not established:

- heterogeneous full/linear model execution;
- full-attention KV transactionality;
- scheduler/ModelRunner metadata wiring;
- checkpoint loading or logit equivalence;
- CUDA atomicity;
- latency, throughput, compression, quality, or memory improvement;
- native Qwen3.5 model support.

The prerequisites now exist for a dependency-light heterogeneous packed layer
stack:

- packed full-attention request isolation;
- packed linear request/state-row isolation;
- cross-layer linear-state transactionality.

The model-stack implementation must avoid the existing packed linear wrapper's
per-layer commit path. It should gather all linear layers through the
coordinator, execute the full layer schedule with candidate states held
locally, and call one cross-layer commit only after every layer succeeds.

The immutable Qwen3.5 schema-v2 canonical result remains `NO_GO`.

## Qwen3.5 Packed Full-Attention Request-Isolation Gate (2026-07-27)

### Why this prerequisite was required

Before building a heterogeneous layer stack, review found that directly
passing all packed request tokens to one full-attention shell would permit
cross-request attention. The packed linear wrapper already isolates state rows,
but full attention needed an explicit token-segment isolation boundary.

Added:

```text
tinyvllm/layers/qwen35_packed_full_decoder_layer.py
tools/test_qwen35_packed_full_decoder_layer.py
```

and:

```text
docs/superpowers/specs/
2026-07-27-qwen35-packed-full-attention-decoder-design.md

docs/superpowers/plans/
2026-07-27-qwen35-packed-full-attention-decoder.md
```

### Request-isolated execution

The wrapper accepts:

```python
forward(
    token_counts: tuple[int, ...],
    position_ids: torch.Tensor,
    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
) -> torch.Tensor
```

For the `(2, 1, 3)` fixture it executes:

```text
full decoder on hidden[0:2]
full decoder on hidden[2:3]
full decoder on hidden[3:6]
concatenate after all segments succeed
```

Position slicing follows the same boundaries for:

```text
[tokens]
[1, tokens]
[3, tokens]
```

The full-attention fixture includes the mean of all tokens visible in one call.
This makes incorrect whole-packed execution observable. Changing request 1/2
tokens by `+10000` leaves request 0 output unchanged, proving request 0 never
sees those tokens.

### Contracts and failure behavior

Validated before layer execution:

- non-empty tuple of positive non-boolean token counts;
- exact sum against packed hidden length;
- rank-two floating hidden states;
- integer positions with rank one or rank two;
- only one or three position rows;
- exact position token width;
- matching position and hidden devices;
- constructor receives a full-attention decoder shell.

BF16 non-contiguous hidden tensors pass for all three position layouts.
A later-request injected attention failure raises without returning a partial
packed output and without mutating inputs.

There is no persistent full-attention KV transaction in this shell. Real paged
KV cache isolation remains a later runtime gate.

## Qwen3.5 Packed Stateful Linear Decoder Gate (2026-07-27)

### Scope and interface

Added:

```text
tinyvllm/layers/qwen35_packed_stateful_decoder_layer.py
tools/test_qwen35_packed_stateful_linear_decoder_layer.py
```

with:

```python
Qwen35PackedStatefulLinearDecoderLayer.forward(
    leases: tuple[HybridStateLease, ...],
    token_counts: tuple[int, ...],
    position_ids: torch.Tensor,
    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
) -> torch.Tensor
```

The wrapper is dependency-light and CPU-only. It does not connect scheduler
sequence metadata, ModelRunner model construction, checkpoint loading, or GPU
kernels.

Written artifacts:

```text
docs/superpowers/specs/
2026-07-27-qwen35-packed-stateful-linear-decoder-design.md

docs/superpowers/plans/
2026-07-27-qwen35-packed-stateful-linear-decoder.md
```

### Packed request mapping

The main fixture uses three requests with unequal token counts:

```text
leases:       (request 0, request 1, request 2)
token_counts: (2, 1, 3)
packed tokens: 6
```

Execution is:

```text
gather_batch once
request 0 hidden[0:2] + state row 0
request 1 hidden[2:3] + state row 1
request 2 hidden[3:6] + state row 2
commit_batch once
```

Out-of-slot-order leases `(slot 2, slot 0, slot 1)` prove that mapping follows
the supplied lease order rather than physical slot order.

The wrapper validates:

- non-empty tuples of leases and token counts;
- matching batch sizes;
- positive non-boolean integer token counts;
- exact token-count sum;
- rank-two floating hidden states;
- integer position IDs with one or three rows and exact packed token width;
- matching hidden/position devices.

Position IDs are preserved as a uniform decoder-layer boundary but are not
consumed by linear attention.

### Transaction and isolation proof

All state rows are gathered before execution. Every request segment runs:

```text
input norm
linear-attention mixer with only its matching state row
first residual
post-attention norm
MLP
second residual
candidate row validation
```

No pool write occurs while request segments are running. Candidate rows are
stacked and sent to exactly one `commit_batch()` only after all requests
succeed.

Tests prove:

- packed hidden output equals an independent per-request oracle;
- every committed state row equals its own request oracle;
- BF16 and non-contiguous packed hidden inputs preserve mapping;
- later-request mixer failure leaves all pool rows unchanged;
- malformed candidate state fails before batch assembly and before commit;
- injected fifth-copy commit failure rolls back the full three-request batch;
- hidden and position inputs are not mutated.

This is sequential per-request correctness execution over packed storage. It
does not claim vectorized or fused multi-request kernel execution.

## Qwen3.5 Batched Layer-State Transaction Gate (2026-07-27)

### Scope

Extended the existing rank-local adapter:

```text
tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_layer_state.py
```

with:

```python
gather_batch(
    leases: tuple[HybridStateLease, ...],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]

commit_batch(
    leases: tuple[HybridStateLease, ...],
    convolution_states: torch.Tensor,
    recurrent_states: torch.Tensor,
) -> None
```

The existing single-request `gather()` and `commit()` interfaces and tests
remain unchanged.

Written design and plan:

```text
docs/superpowers/specs/
2026-07-27-qwen35-batched-layer-state-transaction-design.md

docs/superpowers/plans/
2026-07-27-qwen35-batched-layer-state-transaction.md
```

No packed decoder, ModelRunner model construction, checkpoint traversal, GPU
process, or remote execution was added.

### Ordered gather semantics

`gather_batch()` requires a non-empty tuple of unique valid leases. It validates
the whole lease batch before reading component state and preserves lease order
in the leading batch dimension.

The three-slot fixture gathers:

```text
(slot 2, slot 0)
```

and verifies output order:

```text
batch row 0 == pool slot 2
batch row 1 == pool slot 0
```

`torch.stack` produces contiguous independent storage. Mutating gathered
convolution or recurrent tensors does not mutate the pool.

### All-batch commit semantics

`commit_batch()`:

1. validates the complete lease tuple;
2. rejects duplicate slot IDs;
3. validates complete convolution and recurrent candidate tensors;
4. snapshots every selected row;
5. copies convolution then recurrent state for each lease in input order;
6. restores all selected rows if any copy raises.

The validation contract requires exact:

```text
[batch, *convolution_component_shape]
[batch, *recurrent_component_shape]
dtype
device
```

Non-tensor candidates also fail before writes.

The success test commits slots 2 and 0 while proving slot 1 remains unchanged.
The rollback test injects failure on the fourth copy:

```text
slot 2 convolution: copied
slot 2 recurrent: copied
slot 0 convolution: copied
slot 0 recurrent: injected failure
```

After the exception, both selected rows and the unselected row match their
pre-commit snapshots.

Repeated single-request `commit()` was deliberately rejected because it could
leave an earlier request committed when a later request fails.

### TDD evidence

The expected RED was:

```text
AttributeError:
'Qwen35LayerStateAdapter' object has no attribute 'gather_batch'
```

The focused GREEN marker was:

```text
qwen35 layer state adapter tests passed
```

Coverage now includes:

- ordered out-of-slot-order gather;
- contiguous clone isolation;
- selected-row commit and unselected-row preservation;
- stale later lease with no partial write;
- empty, list, non-lease, and duplicate-slot rejection;
- candidate tensor, batch-size, component-shape, dtype, and device rejection;
- late multi-row copy failure with complete rollback;
- all prior single-request gather/commit behavior.

## Qwen3.5 Stateful Linear Decoder-Layer Transaction Gate (2026-07-26)

### Scope

Added the next dependency-light CPU correctness gate:

```text
tinyvllm/layers/qwen35_stateful_decoder_layer.py
tools/test_qwen35_stateful_linear_decoder_layer.py
```

The new `Qwen35StatefulLinearDecoderLayer` composes:

```text
Qwen35DecoderLayerShell
Qwen35LinearAttentionShell-compatible mixer
Qwen35LayerStateAdapter
```

It deliberately does not connect ModelRunner, checkpoint loading, packed
multi-request batches, or GPU execution.

### Transaction order

The tested order is:

```text
gather
input_layernorm
linear_attention
post_attention_layernorm
mlp
commit
```

`gather()` returns clone-isolated convolution and recurrent state. The wrapper
finishes both residual paths and validates the final MLP output before calling
`commit()`. It returns the hidden output only after commit succeeds.

Therefore:

- stale leases fail before any decoder component runs;
- input-norm, mixer, post-norm, and MLP failures leave the pool unchanged;
- malformed mixer hidden output fails before commit;
- malformed candidate state reaches adapter validation but produces no pool
  write;
- an injected second-copy failure rolls back both pool components;
- position IDs and hidden inputs remain unmodified;
- BF16 and non-contiguous hidden inputs preserve the transaction contract.

The guarantee covers persistent `HybridStateTensorPool` contents. It does not
claim rollback of arbitrary side effects inside injected modules.

before any copy. The test now distinguishes:

```text

invalid candidate state -> commit validation call, no pool mutation
```

## 2026-07-26 Qwen3.5 layer-state pool adapter

### Scope and artifacts

This CPU-only phase added:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-qwen35-layer-state-adapter-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-qwen35-layer-state-adapter.md`;
- `tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_layer_state.py`:
  `Qwen35LayerStateAdapter`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_layer_state_adapter.py`.

The adapter targets one rank-local Qwen3.5 linear-attention layer and the
existing `HybridStateTensorPool`. It does not modify ModelRunner or invoke a
GPU.

### Generation-safe gather

`gather(lease)` first calls:

```text
HybridStateTensorPool.validate(lease)
```

so slot id, request id, and generation must match the active tensor-pool
binding. It returns clones of:

```text
linear_convolution
linear_recurrent
```

Callers cannot mutate pool storage through gathered tensors.

### Transactional dual-component commit

`commit()`:

1. validates the lease;
2. validates convolution and recurrent candidate shape/dtype/device before
   any write;
3. snapshots both destination rows;
4. copies convolution then recurrent state;
5. restores both snapshots if either copy raises.

The test injects failure on the second copy through the focused
`_copy_component` seam. The first convolution write is rolled back and both
pool components equal their pre-commit values afterward.

Tests also prove:

- successful gather/commit;
- gathered clone storage does not alias pool storage;
- stale generation rejection;
- invalid candidate shape/dtype/device leaves both rows unchanged;
- invalid or missing layer components fail closed.

## 2026-07-26 Qwen3.5 linear-attention shell

### Scope and artifacts

This CPU-only phase completed:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-qwen35-linear-attention-shell-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-qwen35-linear-attention-shell.md`;
- `tinyvllm/layers/gated_delta.py`:
  `qwen35_gated_rmsnorm`;
- `tinyvllm/layers/qwen35_linear_attention.py`:
  `Qwen35LinearAttentionShell`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_gated_delta_reference.py` gated-norm coverage;
- `tools/test_qwen35_linear_attention_shell.py`.

No HybridStateTensorPool write, ModelRunner model selection, packed
multi-request dispatch, checkpoint traversal, CUDA process, or remote GPU
process was added.

### Official operation order

The implementation was audited against:

```text
/tmp/modeling_qwen3_5.py
SHA-256 15d5425ee6e771f8fbca10468c280fe62afa79fab3eff73ad1a8852162799d48
```

The dependency-light shell executes:

```text
in_proj_qkv
in_proj_z
in_proj_b
in_proj_a
causal depthwise convolution
Q/K/V split
Q/K head repeat when value_heads > key_heads
gated-delta recurrent update
RMSNorm before SiLU(z) gate
out_proj
return output and candidate states
```

The official gated normalization formula is:

```text
normalized = core * rsqrt(mean(core^2) + eps)
scaled = norm_weight * normalized
gated = scaled * silu(z)
```

`qwen35_gated_rmsnorm` performs normalization and gate math in FP32, returns
to the core dtype, and fails closed on shape/dtype/device/epsilon contracts.

### Shape and orientation evidence

The main fixture deliberately uses:

```text
local_key_heads = 1
local_value_heads = 2
key_head_dim = 2
value_head_dim = 3
```

so the test cannot accidentally pass by assuming key/value heads or dimensions
are equal.

Projection widths are:

```text
key_width = 2
value_width = 6
conv_width = 10
```

After convolution, query and key are reshaped to one key head and repeated
into two value heads. The physical recurrent state remains:

```text
[local_value_heads, value_head_dim, key_head_dim]
  = [2, 3, 2]
```

The independent oracle explicitly transposes this physical orientation into
mathematical `[head,key_dim,value_dim]` orientation during recurrence.

### Transactional candidate-state semantics

The shell never mutates input persistent state:

```text
convolution_state
recurrent_state
```

The pure primitives return candidates. The shell completes gated normalization
and `out_proj` before returning:

```text
(output, candidate_convolution_state, candidate_recurrent_state)
```

An injected output-projection failure occurs after both candidate states have
been computed and still leaves both input states byte-for-byte unchanged.
Future pool integration must commit candidates only after a successful shell
return.

### TDD and coverage

The intended gated-norm RED was:

```text
AttributeError:
module 'qwen35_gated_delta_test_target'
has no attribute 'qwen35_gated_rmsnorm'
```

The intended shell RED was:

```text
FileNotFoundError:
tinyvllm/layers/qwen35_linear_attention.py
```

The shell's observable call order is:

```text
in_proj_qkv
in_proj_z
in_proj_b
in_proj_a
causal_conv
gated_delta_recurrent
gated_rmsnorm
out_proj
```

Tests prove:

- exact independent numerical equivalence;
- asymmetric state orientation;
- key-head repeat into more value heads;
- one-shot versus split continuation output and state equality;
- FP32 and BF16 behavior;
- hidden/projection weights/input states are not mutated;
- output-projection failure does not commit state;
- constructor dimension, divisibility, epsilon, parameter shape/dtype/device
  failures;
- hidden/convolution/recurrent input shape/dtype/device failures;
- projection rank/token/feature/floating/dtype/device failures;
- malformed convolution and recurrent primitive outputs;
- output projection tensor/rank/token/floating/dtype/device failures.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 native packed model-owner binding

### Scope and artifacts

This CPU/static gate completed:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-native-model-owner-binding-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-native-model-owner-binding.md`;
- `tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_hybrid_model_owner.py`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_native_model_owner_binding.py`;
- `tinyvllm/engine/model_runner.py` owner field and explicit binding methods;
- `tools/test_model_runner_spec_verify.py` dependency-light import stub.

No model-selection, checkpoint-loading, Scheduler-admission, Engine-step
automatic binding, CUDA/NCCL, local GPU, or remote GPU path was added.

### Ownership contract

`build_qwen35_hybrid_model_owner(model)` accepts only the exact
`Qwen35PackedHeterogeneousLayerStack` type and derives:

```text
state_transaction = model.state_transaction
pool = state_transaction.pool
runtime_bridge = HybridStateRuntimeBridge(pool)
```

It creates no `HybridStateTensorPool` and copies no state tensor. Tests compare
the pool tensor storage pointers before and after construction.

The factory rejects:

- non-packed models and packed-stack subclasses;
- transaction subclasses;
- transaction adapter indices that differ from model linear-layer indices;
- adapters that do not all reference the exact transaction pool.

`ModelRunner.bind_qwen35_hybrid_model_owner(owner)` requires:

- the exact `Qwen35HybridModelOwner` type;
- `owner.model is self.model`;
- `model.state_transaction is owner.state_transaction`;
- `state_transaction.pool is owner.pool`;
- `runtime_bridge.pool is owner.pool`;
- no different already-bound model owner or runtime bridge;
- no restore owner or participant from another pool.

All coherence checks happen before mutation. Identical-owner rebinding is
idempotent; replacement and forged ownership graphs fail closed.

`bind_current_qwen35_hybrid_model()` returns the pickle-safe identity row:

```text
participant_id
capacity
layout_fingerprint
bytes_per_slot
linear_layer_indices
```

With the current production constructor it fails before mutation because
`ModelRunner` still builds `Qwen3ForCausalLM`.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 transactional root causal-LM shell

### Scope and artifacts

This CPU/dependency-light gate completed:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-transactional-root-causal-lm-shell-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-transactional-root-causal-lm-shell.md`;
- `tinyvllm/layers/qwen35_packed_layer_stack.py` staged `prepare()` and
  `commit()` APIs;
- `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_packed.py`:
  `Qwen35PackedForCausalLM`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_transactional_root_causal_lm.py`.

No production model selection, checkpoint loading, Engine startup binding,
Scheduler admission, CUDA/NCCL, local GPU, or remote GPU work was added.

### Transaction boundary

The packed heterogeneous stack now exposes:

```text
prepare(leases, token_counts, position_ids, hidden_states)
  -> hidden_states, candidates

commit(leases, candidates)
```

`prepare()` performs gather and all packed full/linear layer execution without
mutating persistent state. Existing `forward()` remains behavior-compatible:

```text
prepare -> commit -> return hidden states
```

The new root shell runs:

```text
validate inputs
embed_tokens, unless input_embeds is supplied
layer_stack.prepare
final_norm
lm_head
layer_stack.commit
return normalized hidden states and logits
```

The lm head test observes the real pool before commit and proves state is still
byte-for-byte unchanged at that point. Therefore recurrent state advances only
after valid logits exist.

### Failure semantics

The focused suite injects failures in:

```text
embedding
packed layer execution
final norm
lm head
cross-layer commit
```

Embedding/layer/norm/head failures never invoke commit and preserve the pool.
Commit failure uses the existing cross-layer snapshots and restores all
convolution and recurrent state.

Malformed embedding, final-norm, and lm-head rank/dtype/width outputs also fail
before mutation. Public leases, token counts, token ids, and input embeddings
are validated before execution.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 root model assembly factory

### Scope and rationale

Added a CPU/static config-driven assembly boundary without prematurely
coupling to TP process groups, CUDA attention backends, or checkpoint names.

Artifacts:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-root-model-assembly-factory-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-root-model-assembly-factory.md`;
- `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_factory.py`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_root_model_assembly_factory.py`.

`assemble_qwen35_packed_model()` consumes:

```text
Qwen3.5 config topology
one existing HybridStateTensorPool
embedding/final norm/lm head modules
strict decoder-layer callback
```

and produces one identity-coherent:

```text
Qwen35PackedModelAssembly
  model
  layer_stack
  state_transaction
  adapters
  pool
```

The factory never constructs a second pool.

### Topology and validation

The config's exact `layer_types` order drives callback invocation. Linear
layers receive one exact adapter for the supplied pool; full-attention layers
receive `None`.

The factory rejects:

- non-exact pool types;
- config/pool linear-layer index mismatch;
- missing convolution or recurrent role;
- state components attached to a full-attention layer;
- callback values that are not exact `Qwen35DecoderLayerShell` instances;
- callback block types that differ from config.

`text_config` wrappers are accepted. Callback failure is local/unpublished and
leaves all pool values unchanged.

```text
full_attention
linear_attention
```

graph, passes its root through `build_qwen35_hybrid_model_owner()`, activates

### Contract change

`qwen35_gated_rmsnorm()` still requires `core` and `gate` to share shape,
dtype, and device. Its rank-one weight must remain floating and colocated, but
may retain a different dtype. Normalization, scale, and SiLU-gate math remain
FP32 and the result returns to `core.dtype`.

`Qwen35LinearAttentionShell` now separates:

```text
compute group: conv_weight, dt_bias
stable group:  A_log, norm_weight
```

The compute group must share one dtype at construction and must match hidden
dtype/device at forward. Stable parameters remain floating and colocated but
are not downcast. All four buffers receive forward-time validation so
post-construction replacement fails closed.

Output and candidate states retain the input compute/state dtypes. The shell
still returns candidates without mutating supplied convolution or recurrent
state.

### Qwen3.5 concrete component factory evidence draft

### Scope and artifacts

Added a config-driven construction gate for the complete checkpoint-bearing
Qwen3.5 graph:

```python
def build_qwen35_concrete_component_assembly(
    hf_config,
    *,
    pool: HybridStateTensorPool,
    tensor_parallel_size: int,
    tensor_parallel_rank: int,
    build_attention_backend: Callable,
    parameter_device: str | torch.device = "meta",
) -> Qwen35ConcreteComponentAssembly
```

Artifacts:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-concrete-component-factory-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-concrete-component-factory.md`;
- `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_components.py`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_concrete_component_factory.py`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_real_component_binding.py`;
- meta-alias hardening in
  `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_checkpoint_binding.py`;
- meta-alias coverage in
  `tools/test_qwen35_checkpoint_target_binding.py`.

This gate is local CPU/static only. It does not load safetensors payloads,
invoke a destination loader, execute model attention/forward, initialize CUDA,
or connect production runtime selection.

### Concrete graph contract

The factory consumes the verified HF-style config, the already-created
`HybridStateTensorPool`, explicit TP size/rank, and an injected
full-attention backend factory. It constructs every checkpoint-bearing
component:

```text
root:
  VocabParallelEmbedding
  Qwen35OffsetRMSNorm
  ParallelLMHead

every layer:
  Qwen35OffsetRMSNorm x2
  MergedColumnParallelLinear
  RowParallelLinear

linear layers:
  SegmentedColumnParallelLinear
  ColumnParallelLinear x3
  RowParallelLinear
  Qwen35LinearAttentionShell

full layers:
  HeadPairedColumnParallelLinear
  ColumnParallelLinear x2
  Qwen35OffsetRMSNorm x2
  Qwen35PartialInterleavedRotaryEmbedding
  injected attention backend
  RowParallelLinear
```

Checkpoint-bearing parameters and buffers are created on `meta` by default.
This preserves exact module type, registration, TP-local shape, dtype, loader
attribute, and alias information without allocating the approximately 4.5 GB
checkpoint payload.

Compute parameters/buffers remain BF16. Linear-attention `A_log` and
`norm_weight` remain F32. The supplied CPU state pool is reused exactly and
remains the only state owner.

Existing TP layers read distributed rank/world size during construction. The
new factory uses a scoped construction context for the explicit TP arguments
and restores both distributed callables in `finally`; it never initializes a
process group or executes collectives.

### Meta tied-embedding hardening

Independent meta tensors can both expose storage pointer zero. Therefore the
binding planner now requires:

```text
meta embedding/lm-head -> exact same Parameter object
allocated tensors      -> same storage pointer and storage offset
```

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 checkpoint target-binding gate

### Scope

Added a torch-aware but read-only binding planner between the dependency-free
checkpoint tensor plan and an assembled native Qwen3.5 model graph:

```python
def build_qwen35_checkpoint_binding_plan(
    model: Qwen35PackedForCausalLM,
    tensor_plan: Qwen35CheckpointTensorPlan,
    *,
    tensor_parallel_size: int,
    tensor_parallel_rank: int,
) -> Qwen35CheckpointBindingPlan
```

Artifacts:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-checkpoint-target-binding-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-checkpoint-target-binding.md`;
- `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_checkpoint_binding.py`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_checkpoint_target_binding.py`.

This gate does not open safetensors files, materialize source tensors, call a
weight loader, mutate parameters/buffers/state pools, or wire production
runtime execution.

### Binding contract

Stable planner targets are resolved deliberately:

```text
embed_tokens.* -> model.embed_tokens.*
final_norm.*   -> model.final_norm.*
layers.N.*     -> model.layer_stack.layers[N].*
```

Every load binds to an exact registered destination kind:

```text
projection/norm/embedding weights -> Parameter
linear conv/A_log/dt_bias/norm    -> Buffer
```

Concrete component selection is validated against the already tested:

```text
VocabParallelEmbedding
Qwen35OffsetRMSNorm
MergedColumnParallelLinear
RowParallelLinear
SegmentedColumnParallelLinear
ColumnParallelLinear
HeadPairedColumnParallelLinear
Qwen35LinearAttentionShell
```

The planner validates transformed source shape, TP-local destination shape,
destination dtype, custom/default/direct loader kind, component `tp_size` and
`tp_rank`, and layer block type before publishing any record.

### TP and packed evidence

The focused fixture uses one real linear-attention layer plus one real
full-attention layer and all concrete load-bearing modules. Its complete
grammar contains:

```text
root: 2
shared: 5 * 2
linear-specific: 9
full-specific: 6
total bindings: 27
```

For every rank at TP=1 and TP=2, all 27 entries bind successfully.

Gate/up sources share one `MergedColumnParallelLinear.weight` destination.
At TP size `P`, each source has local shape:

```text
[intermediate_size / P, hidden_size]
```

and binds disjoint row slices:

```text
gate: (0, intermediate_size / P)
up:   (intermediate_size / P, intermediate_size / P)
```

The convolution source transform:

```text
[global_conv_width, 1, kernel]
-> squeeze channel
-> [global_conv_width / P, kernel]
```

binds the exact rank-local `conv_weight` buffer.

F32 `A_log` and `norm_weight` destinations remain F32. BF16 compute
parameters/buffers remain BF16. `embed_tokens.weight` and `lm_head.weight`
must share the same storage pointer and storage offset; a copied second
allocation fails closed.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 transactional checkpoint assignment gate

### Scope and artifacts

Added:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-transactional-checkpoint-assignment-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-transactional-checkpoint-assignment.md`;
- `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_checkpoint_assignment.py`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_checkpoint_assignment.py`.

Public API:

```python
def assign_qwen35_checkpoint_tensors(
    binding_plan: Qwen35CheckpointBindingPlan,
    source_tensors: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor],
) -> Qwen35CheckpointAssignmentResult
```

This gate starts from already-materialized CPU tensors. It does not open
checkpoint files, import safetensors, run CUDA, execute model forward, or wire
production ModelRunner/Engine/Scheduler.

### Assignment contract

The executor first prevalidates the complete operation set without mutation:

```text
exact source-name coverage
CPU tensor source values
exact metadata shape and dtype
identity or squeeze_conv_channel transform
CPU non-meta destinations
custom/default/direct loader kind
callable custom loaders
packed-slot rules
direct-buffer TP-local shape
```

Execution uses the existing TP loaders rather than reimplementing parameter
sharding:

```text
VocabParallelEmbedding -> axis-0 vocabulary shard
ColumnParallelLinear -> axis-0 shard
SegmentedColumnParallelLinear -> per-segment local concatenation
HeadPairedColumnParallelLinear -> complete contiguous head-pair shard
MergedColumnParallelLinear -> packed gate/up local slice
RowParallelLinear -> axis-1 shard
```

Default RMSNorm parameters copy the replicated source directly.
Linear-attention buffers use explicit direct-copy preparation:

```text
conv_weight -> squeeze channel, then axis-0 TP shard
A_log -> axis-0 TP shard
dt_bias -> axis-0 TP shard
norm_weight -> replicated
```

### Transaction and rollback evidence

Every unique destination object is snapshotted once before the first write.
This correctly handles the two packed gate/up sources sharing one destination.
Operations then execute in binding-plan order under `torch.no_grad()`.

On any exception, every unique destination is restored from its snapshot
before a contextual assignment error is raised. An injected failure in a late
custom loader proved that all earlier parameter and buffer writes are rolled
back.

```text

unique destinations per rank: 25
```

- vocabulary axis-0 shards;

The prevalidation matrix covers wrong plan/mapping types, missing/extra source,

The default macOS API Kerberos cache was empty and the fixed ControlMaster
socket did not exist, causing:

```text
Connection closed by UNKNOWN port 65535
```

The TRAE SSH wrapper exposed the valid cache:

```text
KRB5CCNAME=FILE:/Users/bytedance/krb5cc_sitian
```

Within one shell lifecycle, a foreground ControlMaster was created at the
fixed path, the preflight was run, and the master was explicitly closed.
This avoids relying on background processes that the tool harness cleans up
between commands.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 binding-aware tiled checkpoint loading gate

### Canonical result

Implemented a CPU/static sub-tensor checkpoint path that never materializes a
complete checkpoint source tensor:

- `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_checkpoint_tiles.py` builds an immutable,
  binding-aware TP-local tile plan;
- `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_checkpoint_tiled_loading.py` constructs a fresh
  unpublished candidate, opens only validated temporary shards, calls
  `get_slice()` rather than `get_tensor()`, materializes one bounded tile,
  copies it directly into its final destination region, and releases it before
  the next tile;
- `tools/test_qwen35_checkpoint_tiles.py` proves all five binding classes and
  exact destination coverage;
- `tools/test_qwen35_real_checkpoint_tiles.py` proves static compatibility for
  all 320 real bindings without opening the real payload;
- `tools/test_qwen35_tiled_checkpoint_loading.py` proves temporary-shard exact
  values, get-slice-only access, custom-loader bypass, one-tile lifetime,
  cleanup, discard, and publication isolation;
- the design and completed plan are
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-binding-aware-tiled-checkpoint-loading-design.md`
  and
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-binding-aware-tiled-checkpoint-loading.md`.

### Exact tile grammar

The verified 320-entry real plan classifies exactly as:

```text
axis-0 local rows: 157
axis-1 local columns: 48
segmented axis-0: 18
squeeze plus axis-0: 18
replicated: 79
unique sources: 320
```

The planner encodes:

- embedding, ordinary column, head-paired query/gate, packed gate/up, `A_log`,
  and `dt_bias` as rank-local axis-0 rows;
- each fused Q/K/V segment as an independent rank-local axis-0 interval;
- MLP, linear-attention, and full-attention output projections as rank-local
  source columns tiled over rows;
- convolution `[channels, 1, kernel]` as direct `[local_channels, kernel]`
  slices using integer selection of the singleton axis;
- RMSNorm and linear-attention norm vectors as replicated one-dimensional
  tiles.

Every binding destination region is covered exactly once. Packed gate/up
bindings cover disjoint slices of their shared destination. The planner rejects
unknown targets, transforms, loader kinds, malformed packed slices,
source-contract conflicts, segmented-owner mismatch, global/local TP-dimension
mismatch, and metadata byte-count mismatch before file I/O.

### Real static budget evidence

Using only the verified real config/index/header and 24-layer meta graph:

```text
TP=1 minimum feasible max_tile_bytes: 12,288
TP=2 minimum feasible max_tile_bytes: 6,144
limiting binding: layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight row tile
```

Fresh exact metrics at those correctness-minimum budgets:

```text
TP=1 rank0: tiles=306,449 destination_bytes=3,763,655,360 peak_tile_bytes=12,288
TP=2 rank0: tiles=426,723 destination_bytes=1,881,935,712 peak_tile_bytes=6,144
TP=2 rank1: tiles=426,723 destination_bytes=1,881,935,712 peak_tile_bytes=6,144
```

Budgets one byte below the boundary fail before payload open. The real static
test guards every `.safetensors` open and passed for all ranks.

These minimum budgets are a correctness lower bound, not a practical loading
default. Hundreds of thousands of Python/safetensors slice operations would
likely impose severe load-time overhead. No load-speed claim follows from this
gate.

### Temporary payload correctness and failure evidence

The two-layer fixture loaded at TP=1 rank0 and TP=2 ranks0/1 with budgets that
force multiple tiles. All 25 unique destinations matched independent
full-source expectations, including embedding aliasing, packed gate/up,
segmented Q/K/V, row-parallel projections, convolution squeeze, replicated
norms, and BF16/F32 buffers.

The test handle makes `get_tensor()` fail immediately and records one
`get_slice()` per requested source. Every callable destination `weight_loader`
is replaced with a failure sentinel; exact loading still succeeds, proving the
tiled path performs direct final-region copies and does not execute
full-source custom loaders.

A weak-reference gate proves each materialized tile is released before the
next copy. The returned candidate retains only owner, binding plan, tile plan,
and scalar stats; it retains no tile tensor mapping.

Failures cover invalid candidate/budget/path, budget below one indivisible
unit, missing source/shard, wrong `get_slice().get_shape()`, wrong materialized
dtype/shape, and injected destination-copy failure. All entered handles close,
no loaded candidate returns, and the partially written candidate remains
private and discardable. A failed tiled load leaves an already occupied
publication slot owner unchanged. The existing publication slot was not
widened to accept tiled candidates and production remains unconnected.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 coalesced tile budget policy gate

### Canonical result

Added a deterministic tile-budget policy over the completed binding-aware tile
planner:

- `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_checkpoint_tile_policy.py` evaluates bounded
  power-of-two budgets, appends an exact non-power-of-two caller cap when
  needed, and returns the first immutable tile plan satisfying the explicit
  tile-count cap;
- `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_checkpoint_tiled_loading.py` now has an internal
  exact-plan loading boundary plus
  `load_qwen35_fresh_checkpoint_candidate_with_tile_policy()`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_checkpoint_tile_policy.py` proves smallest-budget,
  exact-final-cap, validation, failure, determinism, and nonmutation behavior;
- `tools/test_qwen35_real_checkpoint_tile_policy.py` proves the real 320-entry
  policy decisions without payload reads;
- `tools/test_qwen35_policy_tiled_checkpoint_loading.py` proves one factory
  invocation, exact selected-plan identity, exact TP=1/2 values, get-slice-only
  behavior, custom-loader bypass, tile release, pre-open policy failure, and
  load-failure discard;
- the design and completed plan are
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-coalesced-tile-budget-policy-design.md`
  and
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-coalesced-tile-budget-policy.md`.

### Policy contract

Inputs:

```text
exact Qwen35CheckpointBindingPlan
positive max_tile_bytes
positive max_tile_count
```

Candidate budgets are ascending powers of two. If the caller cap is not a
power of two, the exact cap is appended as the final candidate. Budgets below
an indivisible binding row unit are skipped. Every valid candidate uses the
full existing tile planner and records:

```text
max_tile_bytes
tile_count
actual peak_tile_bytes
```

The first candidate satisfying `tile_count <= max_tile_count` wins. If no
budget is feasible, or feasible plans still exceed the count cap, the policy
fails before file I/O with distinct errors.

The policy does not mutate bindings, destinations, model, or state pool and
performs no checkpoint file access.

### Real 320-entry decision evidence

With caller caps:

```text
max_tile_bytes = 16 MiB
max_tile_count = 512
```

fresh static decisions are:

```text
TP=1 rank0: selected 16 MiB, 488 tiles
TP=2 rank0: selected  8 MiB, 488 tiles
TP=2 rank1: selected  8 MiB, 488 tiles
```

The first design draft incorrectly expected both TP sizes to select 16 MiB.
The real gate failed that assertion. The corrected policy is per exact rank
binding plan: TP2 already meets the cap at 8 MiB and must choose the smaller
peak bound.

Boundary evidence:

```text
TP=1 at 8 MiB: 651 tiles -> reject 512 cap
TP=2 at 4 MiB: 651 tiles -> continue
TP=2 at 8 MiB: 488 tiles -> select
```

Every real `.safetensors` payload open is guarded and remained zero.

### Policy-driven load evidence

The policy-driven API invokes the candidate factory exactly once, selects a
plan from that same binding plan, and passes the exact plan object into the
shared loader:

```text
loaded.tile_plan is decision.tile_plan
```

Temporary fixture decisions with `max_tile_bytes=256` and
`max_tile_count=40`:

```text
TP=1 selected 128 bytes
TP=2 selected  64 bytes
```

TP=1 rank0 and TP=2 ranks0/1 matched all independent destination expectations.
The existing get-slice-only proxy, failing custom-loader sentinels, balanced
handle tracking, and weak-reference tile lifetime gates all remain effective.

A policy failure at TP1 `64 bytes / 40 tiles` occurs before any shard opens. An
injected fourth-tile copy failure closes all entered handles, returns no loaded
candidate, leaves the private candidate partially written/discardable, and
still invokes the factory only once.

Refactored `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_checkpoint_assignment.py` around:

```python
def _assign_qwen35_checkpoint_source_bindings(
    bindings: tuple[Qwen35CheckpointTensorBinding, ...],
    source: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    tensor_parallel_size: int,
    tensor_parallel_rank: int,
) -> int
```

The existing public all-source assignment API still performs complete
prevalidation, snapshots every unique destination once, preserves binding-plan
execution order, and restores all destinations after failure. The new internal
primitive shares its transform, TP-loader, packed-slot, direct-buffer, dtype,
shape, and contextual-error rules but intentionally does not snapshot or
rollback because its caller owns a fresh unpublished candidate.

### Streamed fresh-candidate boundary

New public API:

```python
def load_qwen35_fresh_checkpoint_candidate(
    candidate_factory,
    checkpoint_dir,
    *,
    max_tensor_bytes: int,
) -> Qwen35LoadedCheckpointCandidate
```

The loader:

- invokes the factory exactly once and requires an exact packed CPU model plus
  exact binding plan;
- verifies every destination is a registered CPU non-meta tensor owned by that
  candidate model;
- validates unique source metadata, per-source bytes, safe shard paths, and
  all required shard files before the first open;
- groups bindings by unique source and processes shards/source names in
  deterministic order;
- materializes, validates, assigns, and releases one source tensor before
  advancing to the next source;
- retains no source mapping in the result;
- builds `Qwen35HybridModelOwner` only after every source is assigned and every
  safetensors handle has closed.

Temporary two-layer evidence at TP=1 rank 0 and TP=2 ranks 0/1:

```text
sources streamed per rank: 27
bindings assigned per rank: 27
shards opened per rank: 2
qwen35 streamed fresh checkpoint tests passed (4 tests)
```

Independent expected rank-local values passed for all 25 unique destinations,
including tied embedding storage, packed gate/up slices, segmented Q/K/V,
head-paired query/gate rows, row-parallel weights, convolution squeeze,
replicated norms, and BF16/F32 buffers.

A weak-reference gate forces collection before each subsequent assignment and
proved the previous materialized source tensor is no longer live. This
establishes one-source-at-a-time Python tensor retention for the temporary
fixture. `peak_source_bytes` is the largest metadata tensor byte count and
`loaded_bytes` is the sum of unique source byte counts.

This does not prove total process RSS. Candidate destinations, temporary views
inside custom loaders, safetensors internals, and allocator behavior are not
included in `peak_source_bytes`.

### Failure discard and publication evidence

The stream failure matrix covers:

- malformed factory/result/budget;
- non-CPU destination;
- destination not owned by the candidate model;
- conflicting source contracts;
- over-budget individual source before any open;
- missing directory/shard/source;
- wrong source shape or dtype;
- injected late custom-loader failure.

All entered shard handles close. A late loader failure leaves an earlier
destination loaded rather than restored, proving the streamed path did not
execute a model-sized rollback. No loaded candidate is returned, so the
partially written model remains private and discardable.

The slot starts empty, accepts only an exact completed loaded candidate,
revalidates the model/layer-stack/transaction/pool graph and runtime-bridge

has no clear or replace method and rejects a second publication while
preserving the first owner.

### Qwen3.5 bounded safetensors reader evidence draft

### Scope and artifacts

Added:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-bounded-safetensors-reader-design.md`;
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-bounded-safetensors-reader.md`;
- `tinyvllm/models/qwen35_checkpoint_reader.py`;
- `tools/test_qwen35_checkpoint_reader.py`.

Public APIs:

```python
materialize_qwen35_checkpoint_sources(
    binding_plan,
    checkpoint_dir,
    *,
    max_materialized_bytes,
) -> Qwen35CheckpointMaterialization

load_and_assign_qwen35_checkpoint(
    binding_plan,
    checkpoint_dir,
    *,
    max_materialized_bytes,
) -> Qwen35CheckpointLoadResult
```

This gate uses only temporary small CPU safetensors shards. It does not read
the real 4.5 GB checkpoint, run CUDA, or connect the generic loader,
ModelRunner, Engine, or Scheduler.

### Reader contract

Before opening any file, the reader validates:

```text
exact binding-plan type
positive non-boolean byte budget
unique source contracts
metadata-derived required byte count
required bytes <= max_materialized_bytes
existing checkpoint directory
safe relative .safetensors shard names
existing required shard files
```

It groups only requested language-model sources by shard, opens each required
shard once with `safe_open(..., framework="pt", device="cpu")`, and calls
`get_tensor()` only for requested names. Extra shard tensors are ignored.

Each loaded tensor must match immutable metadata shape, dtype, CPU device, and
byte count. The complete source mapping is published only after all shard
context managers exit, using `MappingProxyType`.

The combined API crosses into the completed transactional assignment executor
only after complete materialization and handle cleanup.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 synthetic tile-copy calibration gate

### Canonical result

Added and ran a correctness-checked, CPU-only safetensors tile-copy
microbenchmark:

- `tools/benchmark_qwen35_safetensors_tile_copy.py` generates one temporary
  BF16 tensor, saves it to a temporary safetensors shard, compares a symmetric
  `get_tensor()+copy_` baseline with complete `get_slice()+copy_` row tiles,
  validates full destination checksums outside timing, and emits a stable
  JSON-serializable result;
- `tools/test_qwen35_synthetic_tile_copy_calibration.py` proves tiny-matrix
  schema/accounting, complete checksum coverage, a short final tile, invalid
  inputs, Apple CPU metadata, CLI execution, and atomic JSON persistence
  without asserting timing order;
- the design and completed plan are
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-synthetic-tile-copy-calibration-design.md`
  and
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-synthetic-tile-copy-calibration.md`;
- the default evidence is
  `experiments/qwen35_hybrid_state/20260727-synthetic-tile-copy-calibration.json`.

The harness creates no GPU work, opens no real checkpoint, and has no
ModelRunner, Engine, Scheduler, state-pool, or production wiring.

### Method and correctness

Default source:

```text
name: synthetic.weight
dtype: bfloat16
shape: [16384, 2048]
payload bytes: 67,108,864
row bytes: 4,096
source checksum: 274,758,369,280.0
```

Host/runtime:

```text
CPU: Apple M5 Pro
Python: 3.12.13
PyTorch: 2.12.0
safetensors: 0.7.0
platform: macOS-26.4.1-arm64-arm-64bit
```

Every baseline and tiled case ran one warm-up plus five timed repeats. Every
timed repeat allocated a full destination, opened the temporary CPU shard,
copied the complete payload, closed the handle, and then computed a full FP32
destination checksum outside the timed region.

Independent artifact validation proved:

```text
schema: qwen35.synthetic-safetensors-tile-copy.v1
all raw repeat counts: 5
all destination checksums exact: YES
all checksum_verified flags: true
all call counts match ceil(rows / rows_per_tile): YES
all peak_tile_bytes <= requested_tile_bytes: YES
printed JSON equals persisted JSON: YES
```

The tiny test case also forces a two-call layout with a one-row final tile,
proving the final short tile is copied and included in the exact checksum.

### Host-local calibration evidence

Final warm-cache medians:

```text
full get_tensor()+copy_ baseline: 2.034791 ms

tile budget  calls  median ms  ratio to baseline
1 MiB          64    3.898667       1.9160
2 MiB          32    2.803500       1.3778
4 MiB          16    2.245542       1.1036
8 MiB           8    1.993333       0.9796
16 MiB          4    1.872958       0.9205
32 MiB          2    1.780166       0.8749
64 MiB          1    1.709583       0.8402
```

On this one host and one contiguous 64 MiB row-sliced tensor, 1-4 MiB tiles
show measurable per-call overhead. Eight MiB is already near the symmetric
full-copy baseline. Larger tiles continue to reduce the median, but the
absolute gain per doubling is small after 16 MiB:

```text
8 -> 16 MiB: 0.120375 ms
16 -> 32 MiB: 0.092792 ms
32 -> 64 MiB: 0.070583 ms
```

This supports retaining the current real-plan policy candidates in the
8-16 MiB region:

```text
TP=1 rank0: 16 MiB / 488 predicted tiles
TP=2 rank0:  8 MiB / 488 predicted tiles
TP=2 rank1:  8 MiB / 488 predicted tiles
```

It does not establish that those values are optimal for a real checkpoint.
The benchmark covers one contiguous axis-0 shape, warm page cache, one local
CPU, and a 64 MiB payload. The real plan mixes five binding classes, 320
sources, multiple shards, and approximately 3.76 GB of TP=1 destination data.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 five-binding synthetic replay calibration gate

### Canonical result

Added and ran a CPU-only planner-driven safetensors replay benchmark covering
all five verified Qwen3.5 checkpoint tile grammars:

- `tools/benchmark_qwen35_five_binding_tile_replay.py` constructs independent
  exact binding plans for `axis0`, `axis1`, `segmented_axis0`,
  `squeeze_axis0`, and `replicated`, asks the existing public tile planner for
  every source/destination slice, and replays those slices against temporary
  safetensors shards;
- `tools/test_qwen35_five_binding_tile_replay.py` proves all five kinds,
  reduced exact schema/accounting, complete TP=2 rank1 destination equality,
  deterministic BF16-exact source values, invalid inputs, focused imports that
  do not load the production engine, CLI execution, and atomic JSON
  persistence without asserting timing order;
- the design and completed plan are
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-five-binding-synthetic-replay-design.md`
  and
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-five-binding-synthetic-replay.md`;
- the evidence is
  `experiments/qwen35_hybrid_state/20260727-five-binding-synthetic-tile-replay.json`.

The harness creates no real model, pool, runner, engine, scheduler, or
publication object. It opens only temporary generated shards on CPU.

### Exact replay contract

Every default case uses:

```text
tensor parallel size: 2
tensor parallel rank: 1
local destination bytes: 33,554,432
tile budgets: 4, 8, 16, 32 MiB
warm-ups: 1 per case/budget
timed repeats: 3 per case/budget
dtype: BF16
```

Axis-sharded sources are 64 MiB because the 32 MiB local rank1 destination is
selected from a TP=2 global source. The replicated source is 32 MiB. Source
integers remain in the exact BF16 range.

The segmented case owns a real `SegmentedColumnParallelLinear` with three
segments. All plans are produced only through:

```python
build_qwen35_checkpoint_tile_plan(
    binding_plan,
    max_tile_bytes=requested_tile_bytes,
)
```

Each replay resets the final destination, opens the temporary shard, obtains
one `PySafeSlice`, materializes every planner-provided source slice, copies
into the exact planner-provided destination slice, closes the handle, and then
requires complete `torch.equal()` destination equality outside timing.

Independent artifact validation proved:

```text
schema: qwen35.five-binding-synthetic-tile-replay.v1
case kinds/order: exact
all local destination bytes: 32 MiB
all repeat counts: 3
all peak_tile_bytes <= requested_tile_bytes: YES
all destination checksums exact: YES
all exact_destination_verified flags: true
persisted JSON equals printed JSON: YES
```

### Host-local grammar-sensitive evidence

Environment:

```text
CPU: Apple M5 Pro
Python: 3.12.13
PyTorch: 2.12.0
safetensors: 0.7.0
platform: macOS-26.4.1-arm64-arm-64bit
```

Final median milliseconds:

```text
kind               4 MiB    8 MiB   16 MiB   32 MiB
axis0             1.7850   1.4620   1.1517   1.1288
axis1             2.6177   2.3740   2.3205   2.1890
segmented_axis0   1.6544   1.4360   1.2348   1.4433
squeeze_axis0     1.6677   1.5772   1.4650   1.4152
replicated        1.5569   1.2967   1.1785   1.1319
```

Median across the five grammar cases:

```text
4 MiB:  1.667667 ms
8 MiB:  1.462041 ms
16 MiB: 1.234833 ms
32 MiB: 1.415209 ms
```

Tile counts for non-segmented cases halve from `8 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1`.
Segment boundaries constrain the segmented case to:

```text
4 MiB: 8 tiles
8 MiB: 4 tiles
16 MiB: 3 tiles
32 MiB: 3 tiles, actual peak still 16 MiB
```

Therefore 32 MiB cannot coalesce that case further and its observed median is
worse than 16 MiB. Axis1 slicing is consistently slower than equal-byte axis0
or replicated copies, showing that one axis0-only calibration is not enough.

The evidence supports:

- reject 4 MiB as unnecessarily call-heavy for these representatives;
- retain 8 MiB as a bounded lower policy candidate;
- prefer 16 MiB as the host-local synthetic diminishing-return point;
- do not raise the global cap to 32 MiB from synthetic evidence alone.

No production policy constant changed. The existing real-plan decisions
remain:

```text
TP=1 rank0: 16 MiB / 488 predicted tiles
TP=2 rank0:  8 MiB / 488 predicted tiles
TP=2 rank1:  8 MiB / 488 predicted tiles
```

The five-binding result suggests evaluating a lower tile-count cap or
kind-weighted policy model before changing TP2 from 8 to 16 MiB, but it does
not by itself justify the additional peak bound.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 weighted tile-policy estimator gate

### Canonical result

Added and ran a deterministic static estimator that combines the real
320-binding Qwen3.5 tile distributions with per-kind fits from the completed
five-binding synthetic replay:

- `tools/estimate_qwen35_weighted_tile_policy.py` validates the calibration
  artifact, fits one `32 MiB byte-copy intercept + per-tile slope` model per
  grammar, applies the fits to exact real static plans, and reports per-kind
  contributions, baseline deltas, incremental comparisons, and Pareto
  dominance;
- `tools/test_qwen35_weighted_tile_policy_estimator.py` proves exact OLS math,
  contribution scaling, Pareto dominance, malformed calibration rejection,
  CLI persistence, and zero payload opens under a hard environment guard;
- the design and completed plan are
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-qwen35-weighted-tile-policy-estimator-design.md`
  and
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-qwen35-weighted-tile-policy-estimator.md`;
- the evidence is
  `experiments/qwen35_hybrid_state/20260727-weighted-tile-policy-estimator.json`.

No production selector, tiled loader, ModelRunner, Engine, Scheduler, owner,
pool, or publication code changed for this gate.

### Fit and estimator contract

The estimator consumes the exact SHA256-bound calibration artifact:

```text
schema: qwen35.five-binding-synthetic-tile-replay.v1
sha256: 21e3edfbb60fa1fa6338906fd147a1b83bce575c88c5499d575927c22c3f3155
budgets: 4, 8, 16, 32 MiB
local bytes per grammar case: 32 MiB
```

For each grammar:

```text
synthetic median seconds =
    intercept for 32 MiB copied
    + per-tile slope * tile count
```

The fitted records are:

```text
kind               intercept ms/32MiB  slope us/tile  R^2
axis0                    1.012456          98.512     0.9756
axis1                    2.161648          56.974     0.9674
segmented_axis0          1.162842          62.070     0.7436
squeeze_axis0            1.397424          35.695     0.9497
replicated               1.060638          61.427     0.9978
```

The segmented fit has the weakest `R^2` because its 16 and 32 MiB plans both
have three segment-constrained tiles while the three-repeat medians fluctuate.
The artifact preserves residuals and does not treat the proxy as measured or
predicted real-load time.

For every real plan kind:

```text
proxy contribution =
    intercept * real destination bytes / 32 MiB
    + slope * real tile count
```

The estimator reads only the verified config/index/header and builds the
24-layer meta binding graph. A `builtins.open` guard counted and failed any
`.safetensors` payload open:

```text
payload_open_count: 0
```

### Real static trade-off evidence

TP=1 rank0:

```text
budget  tiles  latency proxy  reduction vs 8 MiB  extra peak vs 8 MiB
4 MiB   1096    0.234185 s        -19.30%             -4 MiB
8 MiB    651    0.196302 s          0.00%              0 MiB
16 MiB   488    0.182239 s          7.16%             +8 MiB
32 MiB   386    0.173188 s         11.78%            +24 MiB
```

Incremental:

```text
8 -> 16 MiB: proxy -7.16%, tiles -163, peak +8 MiB
16 -> 32 MiB: proxy -4.97%, tiles -102, peak +16 MiB
```

TP=2 rank0 and rank1 are identical:

```text
budget  tiles  latency proxy  reduction vs 8 MiB  extra peak vs 8 MiB
4 MiB    651    0.124714 s        -12.71%             -4 MiB
8 MiB    488    0.110650 s          0.00%              0 MiB
16 MiB   386    0.101599 s          8.18%             +8 MiB
32 MiB   371    0.100121 s          9.52%            +24 MiB
```

Incremental:

```text
8 -> 16 MiB: proxy -8.18%, tiles -102, peak +8 MiB
16 -> 32 MiB: proxy -1.45%, tiles  -15, peak +16 MiB
```

Every candidate is on the two-dimensional peak/proxy Pareto frontier: smaller
budgets reduce the explicit materialization bound while larger budgets reduce
the modeled call overhead. There is no universally dominating budget.

### Policy interpretation

The current count-only selector with:

```text
max_tile_bytes = 16 MiB
max_tile_count = 512
```

still selects:

```text
TP=1 rank0: 16 MiB / 488 tiles
TP=2 rank0:  8 MiB / 488 tiles
TP=2 rank1:  8 MiB / 488 tiles
```

The estimator strengthens the case for including 16 MiB in a future TP2
real-load comparison: it models an 8.18% proxy reduction for only +8 MiB peak.
It does not support raising the cap to 32 MiB before real evidence: TP2 gains
only another 1.45% proxy while spending another +16 MiB peak and removing just
15 tiles.

No production default changed. Changing the TP2 count cap from 512 toward 386
would force 16 MiB, but doing so from a synthetic proxy would violate the
current evidence boundary.
