## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 hybrid prefix exact tensor interning

Added an exact, cache-local content-addressed tensor store to:

```text
tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_hybrid_prefix_cache.py
```

Design and execution records:

```text
docs/superpowers/specs/
  2026-07-27-qwen35-hybrid-prefix-exact-tensor-interning-design.md
docs/superpowers/plans/
  2026-07-27-qwen35-hybrid-prefix-exact-tensor-interning.md
```

The implementation interns detached contiguous snapshot tensors using:

```text
dtype
shape
device type/index
SHA-256 of logical contiguous bytes
exact contiguous uint8 byte-view equality
```

The digest is only a bucket selector. Exact byte equality is mandatory before
sharing, so forced digest collisions do not alias different values or
different floating-point representations such as `+0.0` and `-0.0`.
Each candidate tensor is hashed once per publication; the prepared intern key
is reused for unique-footprint and intern-table lookup.

Each snapshot still reports its logical referenced `storage_bytes`. Cache
budgeting now uses unique canonical physical tensor storage:

```text
current_bytes: unique canonical storage
current_logical_bytes: all entry references
deduplicated_bytes: logical minus unique
```

Lifecycle coverage proves:

```text
different prefixes can share identical canonical tensor objects/data_ptrs
source pool mutation cannot change canonical values
partial equality shares only matching tensors
replacement updates refcounts without leaks
remove/invalidate/clear retain storage until the final reference
intern failure after one acquired ref rolls back that ref
forced digest collisions remain byte-exact
max_bytes is enforced on unique physical storage
LRU eviction remains deterministic
acquire and cross-layer rollback semantics remain unchanged
```

Focused CPU fixture measurements for two different prefixes published from the
same state row:

```text
FP32:
  entries: 2
  logical referenced bytes: 224
  unique physical snapshot bytes: 112
  deduplicated bytes: 112
  retained-storage ratio: 2.00x

BF16:
  entries: 2
  logical referenced bytes: 112
  unique physical snapshot bytes: 56
  deduplicated bytes: 56
  retained-storage ratio: 2.00x
```

These values are exact fixture-level cache-owned tensor accounting. They are
not evidence of production hit rate, process RSS, CUDA allocated/reserved
memory, KV-cache reduction, TTFT, throughput, or end-to-end speedup.

### Cache-local staged publication prerequisite

Before an all-rank publication transaction can be safe, cache capture must be
separated from visibility. Added:

```text
Qwen35HybridPrefixPreparedPublication
Qwen35HybridPrefixSnapshotCache.prepare_publication()
Qwen35HybridPrefixSnapshotCache.commit_publication()
Qwen35HybridPrefixSnapshotCache.rollback_publication()
```

The cache permits one private prepared snapshot at a time:

```text
prepare:
  validates, clones, hashes once, and holds state privately
commit:
  interns and publishes atomically
rollback:
  drops the private clones without changing visible entries
```

Existing `publish()` now composes prepare plus commit and preserves its public
semantics.

Fresh proof covers:

```text
prepare does not change visible entries, LRU, or visible bytes
source mutation after prepare cannot change staged values
rollback preserves an older same-key entry
commit consumes the handle and restores exact staged values
foreign/replayed/committed/rolled-back handles reject
one concurrent prepare conflict rejects
oversize prepare creates no live handle
commit interning failure restores refs/counters and leaves the handle
available for explicit rollback
each candidate tensor remains hashed once per publication
```

Observability:

```text
current_prepared_publications
current_prepared_bytes
peak_prepared_bytes
publication_prepares
publication_commits
publication_rollbacks
publication_prepare_conflicts
```

### Engine acknowledged hybrid prefix publication phase transport

The shared-memory ModelRunner command channel broadcasts one argument tuple to
every rank, while publication payloads bind an explicit `participant_id`.
The transport therefore broadcasts the complete immutable rank matrix:

```text
tuple[Qwen35HybridPrefixPublicationPayload, ...]
```

`ModelRunner._qwen35_hybrid_prefix_publication_payload()` now accepts either a
single rank-local payload or the complete matrix. Matrix mode requires exact
world-size length, unique contiguous participant IDs, and selects only
`payloads[self.rank]` before participant delegation.

Engine adds strict matrix/result validators and five acknowledged phase APIs:

```text
prepare_model_runner_hybrid_prefix_publication
precommit_model_runner_hybrid_prefix_publication
finalize_model_runner_hybrid_prefix_publication
seal_model_runner_hybrid_prefix_publication
rollback_model_runner_hybrid_prefix_publication
```

Before dispatch, the matrix is sorted and validated for:

```text
one payload per rank
contiguous participant IDs
equal ticket/request/key/token/block identity
key.tensor_parallel_size == ModelRunner world_size
```

After dispatch, nested rows must have the exact fields:

```text
ticket_id
participant_id
operation
status
detail
```

Outer worker rank and inner participant ID must match exactly. Missing,
duplicate, swapped, malformed, wrong-operation, wrong-status, and non-string
detail rows poison the acknowledgement collector. Valid business outcomes
such as `prepare: rejected` and phase `error` remain ordinary rows and are not
mistaken for transport corruption.

### Engine hybrid prefix publication transaction coordinator

Broadcast rollback required one participant semantic fix first. The Engine
transport cannot target only ranks that prepared successfully, so
`Qwen35HybridPrefixPublicationParticipant.rollback()` now treats the same
payload as an idempotent abort:

```text
prepared/precommitted/finalized -> exact cache rollback -> rolled_back
already rolled_back -> rolled_back
rejected -> rolled_back
unseen ticket -> rolled_back
committed -> error
same ticket with different payload -> error
```

This preserves committed immutability and ticket binding while allowing every
rank to end in a terminal non-visible state after a broadcast abort.

Added:

```text
tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_hybrid_prefix_engine_publication.py
Qwen35HybridPrefixEnginePublicationCoordinator
Qwen35HybridPrefixEnginePublicationTransaction
tools/test_engine_hybrid_prefix_publication_transaction.py
```

The explicit coordinator flow is:

```text
validate payload matrix
prepare all ranks
  any rejected -> rollback all ranks -> return false
  any error -> rollback all ranks -> raise
precommit all ranks
  any error -> rollback all ranks -> raise
finalize all ranks
  any error -> rollback all ranks -> raise
seal all ranks
  any error -> poison/fail-stop
success -> committed
```

Rollback requires `rolled_back` from every rank. A rollback error, malformed
row, or rollback transport exception poisons both the coordinator and Engine
acknowledgement collector. Seal error also poisons. A transport exception in
any phase means completion is uncertain; the coordinator poisons immediately
and does not falsely claim that rollback succeeded.

`LLMEngine` now has only explicit, opt-in control-plane entry points:

```text

publish_qwen35_hybrid_prefix
```

Installation validates coordinator type, exact Engine identity, idempotency,
and replacement rejection.

The eligibility boundary is intentionally strict:

```text
source is a live Sequence
prompt token count is positive and exactly full-block aligned
num_computed_tokens covers the complete prompt

```

after prefill represents the complete prompt; pairing it with a shorter
full-block prefix would be a silent state/token mismatch and violate the
no-loss requirement.

```text
request_id
Qwen35HybridPrefixKey
prompt token tuple
block (id, generation, hash) tuple
HybridStateLease
```

The prompt token slice excludes any sampled first completion token already
appended by Scheduler postprocess. Later Sequence token/block-table mutation
or Block metadata mutation does not mutate the frozen candidate.

`candidate.publication_payloads(ticket_id, world_size)` builds one exact
payload per contiguous rank and rejects TP mismatch. Payload matrices pass

Automatic runtime wiring is currently blocked by one concrete lifecycle
boundary: `Scheduler.postprocess()` both commits prefill block hashes and may
append the first sampled token, mark the request finished, and release its KV
blocks/hybrid-state lease in the same call. An Engine callback after

lacks committed block identities. The next safe gate is a two-stage Scheduler
prefill completion barrier that commits metadata, exposes still-live eligible
sources, and only then finalizes sampling/release.

### Scheduler complete-prefill commit hook

Added a default-off synchronous Scheduler callback:

```text
Scheduler.install_prefill_commit_hook(hook)
Scheduler._notify_prefill_committed(sequence)
tools/test_scheduler_prefill_commit_hook.py
```

The callback runs in legacy, final chunked, and final mixed prefill paths at
the exact ordering boundary:

```text
BlockManager.commit_prefill()
Sequence.num_computed_tokens = complete_prompt_end
prefill_commit_hook(sequence)
append first sampled completion token / finish / release
```

Non-final chunks are suppressed. Successful notifications are deduplicated by
request ID, including the full-prefix-cache-hit last-token logits recompute
case. The same callable may be installed idempotently; replacement or a
non-callable is rejected.

If the callback raises, Scheduler records the exception type/message and
re-raises before token append or resource release. Every later `schedule()`
fails closed with the stored poison reason. The request is recorded as
notified only after the callback returns successfully.

### Canonical Qwen3.5 runtime prefix identity binding

Added:

```text
tinyvllm/engine/qwen35_hybrid_prefix_runtime_identity.py
Qwen35HybridPrefixRuntimeIdentity
validate_qwen35_model_fingerprint()
bind_qwen35_hybrid_prefix_runtime_identity()
ModelRunner.bind_qwen35_hybrid_prefix_runtime_identity()
LLMEngine.configure_qwen35_hybrid_prefix_runtime_identity()
tools/test_qwen35_runtime_prefix_identity_binding.py
```

The canonical identity is:

```text
model_fingerprint
layout_fingerprint
dtype
```

`model_fingerprint` must be a lowercase 64-character SHA256 supplied by the
verified checkpoint-manifest boundary. A model path or arbitrary label is not
accepted. Runtime does not scan all weight tensors to invent an identity.

`layout_fingerprint` is derived only from the bound owner's
`pool.layout.fingerprint`. `dtype` is derived from the same layout and requires
all recurrent-state components to use one identical supported dtype. Mixed
component dtypes fail closed because the current cache key has one dtype
field.

ModelRunner binds the immutable identity once to the exact current
`Qwen35HybridModelOwner`. Repeating the same SHA256 is idempotent. A different
SHA256 or replacing the owner object after identity binding fails closed.
Rank rows transport canonical dtype names (`float16`, `bfloat16`, `float32`).

Engine sends the manifest SHA256 through the acknowledged ModelRunner command
path and validates:

```text
one row per contiguous rank
inner participant ID equals outer rank
exact row field schema
all-rank model/layout/dtype equality
returned model SHA256 equals requested SHA256
```

Malformed or inconsistent identity poisons the acknowledgement collector and
leaves Engine identity unset.

```text
model_fingerprint=<lowercase 64-character SHA256>
```

```text
owner
```

leave both unchanged; successful one-shot publication preserves the exact
candidate owner and fingerprint.

repeating a magic value at every call site, while dedicated invalid cases call

```text
ModelRunner.bind_qwen35_loaded_checkpoint_candidate(candidate)
```

```text
bound owner is candidate.owner by object identity
identity owner is candidate.owner by object identity
bound identity equals candidate-derived identity
```

Partial pre-existing owner-only or identity-only state is rejected rather than
implicitly upgraded. A different candidate is rejected without replacing the
original binding.

## 2026-07-27 Engine resumable prefix publication runtime configuration

Implemented the explicit Engine entry point:

```text
LLMEngine.configure_qwen35_hybrid_prefix_publication_runtime(
    *,
    model_fingerprint,
    max_entries,
    max_bytes,
    timeout_s,
)
```

The method prevalidates the full request and every existing child state before
mutation. It then composes these already proven stages in strict order:

```text
configure restore owner/coordinator
configure canonical all-rank runtime identity
create/install Engine publication coordinator
install identity-driven Scheduler source publisher
store aggregate completion only after all stages succeed
```

Completed exact repeat revalidates every child configuration/object pair and
returns the stable installed publisher without invoking child stages. A
conflicting aggregate or child state fails before child calls. Restore,
identity, coordinator, publisher, and aggregate state each require coherent
configuration/object pairs.

Later-stage failure deliberately leaves completed exact child stages installed
without aggregate completion. Exact retry therefore resumes safely through
the child methods' existing idempotency:

```text
coordinator install failure:
  restore + identity retained
  exact retry recreates coordinator and completes
publisher install failure:
  restore + identity + coordinator retained
  exact retry reuses coordinator and completes
```

## 2026-07-27 Engine all-rank loaded checkpoint candidate binding

Added a local-only candidate handoff boundary:

```text
Qwen35HybridModelOwnerPublicationSlot.candidate
ModelRunner.publish_qwen35_loaded_checkpoint_candidate(candidate)
ModelRunner.bind_published_qwen35_loaded_checkpoint_candidate()
```

The one-shot slot now stores one publication tuple containing the exact
candidate, owner, and verified model-manifest fingerprint. All three fields
remain absent until owner-graph validation completes, then become visible
together through one tuple assignment.

Every ModelRunner owns one local candidate slot. A future checkpoint worker
must load and publish the candidate inside that rank's process. Engine never
serializes the candidate or model owner through shared memory.

The zero-argument ModelRunner bind method reads its local candidate and invokes
the previously proven atomic owner+runtime-identity binder. It returns:

```text
operation=bind_loaded_checkpoint_candidate
status=bound | error
participant_id
model_fingerprint
layout_fingerprint
dtype
detail
```

Expected missing/conflicting candidate errors are returned as `error` rows
instead of raising through the acknowledgement transport. Exact retry can
therefore converge after the local rank is repaired. Base exceptions and
uncertain transport failures remain governed by the existing fail-stop
acknowledgement collector.

Added the explicit Engine entry point:

```text
LLMEngine.bind_qwen35_loaded_checkpoint_candidates(timeout_s=...)
```

It broadcasts only:

```text
bind_published_qwen35_loaded_checkpoint_candidate()
```

with zero positional payload arguments. It validates one exact result row per
rank, outer/inner rank agreement, operation/status/detail schema, canonical
lowercase SHA256 model fingerprint, supported dtype, and homogeneous
model/layout/dtype provenance across all ranks.

A participant `error` leaves aggregate completion unset and does not poison
the acknowledged transport. Successful ranks remain idempotently bound; exact
retry reissues the zero-payload command. Aggregate rows/configuration are
stored only after every rank returns `bound`. Completed exact repeat revalidates
the full stored rank matrix and returns it without dispatch.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 rank checkpoint candidate target factory

Implemented:

```text
prepare_qwen35_checkpoint_candidate_target(
    hf_config,
    tensor_plan,
    *,
    pool,
    tensor_parallel_size,
    tensor_parallel_rank,
    build_attention_backend,
    parameter_device="meta",
)
```

The factory composes the existing concrete Qwen3.5 component assembly and
exact checkpoint binding planner into one rank-local prepared target. It
returns a one-shot `take()` result matching the existing streamed/tiled loader
contract:

```text
(exact Qwen35PackedForCausalLM, exact Qwen35CheckpointBindingPlan)
```

The supplied `HybridStateTensorPool` remains the sole state pool. The factory
contains zero `HybridStateTensorPool(...)` allocations, verifies exact pool
identity through the assembled graph, validates pool layout against config and
TP, and preserves valid wider speculative convolution state. It derives the
existing speculative-token width from the supplied immutable layout and
constructs only a canonical layout description for fingerprint comparison.

The factory also verifies:

```text
assembly TP size/rank == requested TP size/rank
binding-plan TP size/rank == requested TP size/rank
every binding destination is the exact registered model tensor
every destination device == assembly parameter_device
pool layout/capacity/device/bindings/storage identity/version unchanged
```

`take()` is one-shot. A second call raises before returning the model or
binding plan, preventing accidental reuse after a loader may have partially
assigned the target.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 authorized prepared-target loader adapter

Implemented:

```text
build_qwen35_authorized_checkpoint_candidate_loader(
    prepare_target,
    *,
    authorization_sha256,
)
```

The result is a frozen callable
`Qwen35AuthorizedCheckpointCandidateLoader`. It validates the exact bounded
request and authorization digest before invoking the target provider. Every
call obtains a fresh exact `Qwen35PreparedCheckpointCandidateTarget`, requires
its parameter device to be CPU, and delegates:

```text
target.take
request.checkpoint_dir
request.max_tensor_bytes
request.model_fingerprint
```

to the existing streamed checkpoint loader.

Fresh-target provisioning is deliberate. A streamed load can fail after
assigning some destinations, so exact retry must never reuse the consumed or
partially assigned model. The adapter stores no target or completion state;
each invocation calls the provider again. ModelRunner's existing outer
completion/publication state remains authoritative.

The adapter returns the exact existing
`Qwen35LoadedCheckpointCandidate` unchanged. It does not adapt tiled candidate
wrapper types because ModelRunner currently requires that exact streamed
candidate type.

## 2026-07-27 Qwen3.5 bounded checkpoint metadata reader

Implemented:

```text
read_qwen35_checkpoint_metadata(...)
build_qwen35_real_checkpoint_rank_loader_from_metadata(...)
```

The metadata reader validates the retained config/index/shard manifest
composite, reads bounded `config.json` and
`model.safetensors.index.json` bytes, verifies their actual SHA256 values, and
for each declared shard reads only:

```text
8-byte little-endian safetensors header length
exact bounded JSON header bytes
```

It verifies safe normalized relative shard names, unique exact shard identity
values, exact observed shard sizes, index/shard-set equality, positive byte
budgets, short reads, UTF-8/JSON object shape, and header length against both
the configured budget and shard size. It returns a frozen
`Qwen35CheckpointMetadataBundle` with:

```text
recursive config attribute namespace
read-only top-level index/header mappings
verified config/index/composite identities
exact metadata byte count
payload_bytes_read = 0
```

The reader never calls safetensors or torch APIs, mmap, CUDA, network,
subprocess, Engine, or `LLMEngine.step()`. Synthetic tracked-file tests prove
that successful reads stop exactly after each JSON header and before payload
bytes. Malformed prefix/header/JSON cases fail closed without reading beyond
the bounded metadata region.

The worker gained an import-only composition helper. It requires an exact
`Qwen35CheckpointMetadataBundle`, rejects any bundle reporting nonzero payload
bytes before tensor-plan/configuration construction, and forwards only the
bundle's parsed config/index/headers and verified identities to the existing
rank-loader builder. It performs no file read, pool allocation, backend call,
loader call, publication, or execution.

### TP4 READY-Path Native Child Cleanup Hardening

A READY-path code audit found that a native rank startup/runtime exception
only called `terminate()` on processes that had completed `start()`. It did not
join them, escalate to `kill()`, or include a process whose `start()` method
raised after creating the child. That could leave gate-owned workers holding
GPUs after a failed authority attempt.

TDD evidence:

```text

  experiments/qwen35_hybrid_state/qwen35-tp4-ready-cleanup-red-20260729-002547
failure:

focused/full GREEN:
  experiments/qwen35_hybrid_state/qwen35-tp4-ready-cleanup-green-20260729-003430
result:

  complete TP4 preflight suite passed 29 tests
```

Preserved failed test-transport attempts:

```text
qwen35-tp4-ready-cleanup-red-20260729-002300
  incomplete test closure omitted the TP1 dependency
qwen35-tp4-ready-cleanup-red-20260729-002454
  SSH transport failed before test execution
qwen35-tp4-ready-cleanup-green-20260729-002930
  SCP/SSH transport failed before remote staging
qwen35-tp4-ready-cleanup-green-20260729-003124
  focused test passed; full regression exposed error-precedence handling
```

The coordinator now requires each native process wrapper to provide `kill()`.
On any startup or runtime exception it snapshots only child objects that are
still alive, performs:

```text
terminate
bounded join, at most 30 seconds
kill remaining children
bounded join, at most 30 seconds
fail closed if any child remains alive
```

This cleanup applies only to process objects constructed by this gate. It does
not signal, exempt, or otherwise mutate any pre-existing remote process.

## 2026-07-29 Qwen3.5 TP4 Performance/Cache Authority Design Frozen

The post-correctness benchmark authority is specified at:

```text
docs/superpowers/specs/
2026-07-29-qwen35-tp4-hybrid-prefix-performance-cache-authority-design.md

docs/superpowers/plans/
2026-07-29-qwen35-tp4-hybrid-prefix-performance-cache-authority.md
```

The first canonical pair is:

```text
P0 recompute:
  same native Qwen3.5 TP4 Engine source
  hybrid-prefix publication/restore disabled
  complete prompt recomputed

P1 exact_restore:
  same source/model/topology/KV capacity/workload
  exact full-fidelity KV-prefix plus convolution/recurrent state restore
  existing exact tensor interning enabled
```

This first authority deliberately excludes int4, token sparsity, low rank,
Gist layer sharing, speculative decoding, KV offload, scheduler policy, and
CUDA Graph changes. A later compressed candidate must retain P0/P1, use P1 as
its numerical/cache-cost reference, and receive a new correctness gate and
source identity.

The benchmark is hard-bound to three independent authorities:

```text
TP4 real root-logit correctness
cached-continuation correctness
real ModelRunner/LLMEngine correctness
```

All three must be immutable `PASS` evidence before a GPU worker command can be
constructed. Missing prerequisites classify as `BLOCKED_CORRECTNESS`; a
four-GPU preflight failure classifies as `BLOCKED_RESOURCES`.

The frozen benchmark matrix contains:

```text
workloads:
  256-token short control
  1024-token medium reuse
  4096-token long reuse
  2048-token eight-request fan-out
  mismatch/stale-generation/clear controls
execution:
  separate fresh P0/P1 processes
  alternating pair order
  one excluded warmup
  one correctness repetition
  five measured repetitions
```

Raw evidence must include output IDs, correctness logits, TTFT, end-to-end and
decode timing, executed/reused token counts, CUDA memory, KV-capacity parity,
and physical/logical/deduplicated hybrid-cache bytes. An independent verifier
reconstructs every metric and classification without trusting `summary.json`.

### TP4 Benchmark Runner/Worker Execution Boundary

Continued CPU-only work found and fixed a material orchestration mismatch:

```text
frozen authority:
  70 canonical process rows
runner before fix:
  emitted 70 single-case commands
worker before fix:
  each command executed all 7 phase/repetition cases for its policy/workload
invalid direct-wiring consequence:
  490 executions and loss of one-process-per-case isolation
```

The worker now has `run_benchmark_case(...)`, which:

- canonicalizes by all frozen case fields rather than Python dataclass object
  identity;
- executes only the authorized phase and repetition;
- resets peak memory only for measured cases;
- writes one process row and the workload's exact request-row count;
- preserves atomic failure evidence and always closes the injected engine.

The executable worker boundary now also:

- parses the exact runner arguments;
- requires explicit model directory, model manifest, and correctness
  prerequisite paths;
- hashes the actual manifest/prerequisite files before runtime loading;
- requires the frozen canonical model-manifest SHA;
- invokes the full contract prerequisite validator, including all three
  authority artifact and independent-verification hashes;
- rejects a handwritten top-level `{"classification": "PASS"}`;
- binds the model directory to the manifest's `remote_model_dir` or
  `local_path`;
- performs all of the above before lazy Torch/Engine imports.

The runner now requires immutable `WorkerRuntimeArtifacts` and includes the
three runtime artifact paths in every canonical worker command.

### TP4 All-Rank Cache and Memory Accounting

The benchmark worker no longer treats rank-zero observations as the TP4
memory/cache total.

Production APIs:

```text
ModelRunner.qwen35_hybrid_prefix_cache_snapshot()
LLMEngine.qwen35_hybrid_prefix_cache_snapshots(timeout_s=...)
LLMEngine.memory_snapshots(timeout_s=...)
aggregate_tp4_cache_snapshots(rows)
aggregate_tp4_memory_snapshots(rows)
```

The Engine transports both observations through the acknowledged ModelRunner
command channel and requires exactly one result for every contiguous rank in
`0..world_size-1`. Payload rank mismatches, duplicate ranks, missing ranks,
wrong schemas, booleans, negative counters, and non-integer counters fail
closed.

Worker aggregation:

```text
cache byte fields:
  current_bytes
  current_logical_bytes
  deduplicated_bytes
  peak_bytes
  => sum across all four ranks

cache replicated counters:
  current_entries
  peak_entries
  hits
  misses
  evictions
  validation_failures
  failed_restores
  => require exact rank parity, then report one value

memory byte fields:
  cuda_allocated_bytes
  cuda_reserved_bytes
  cuda_peak_allocated_bytes
  cuda_peak_reserved_bytes
  kv_capacity_bytes
  => sum across all four ranks
```

This prevents rank-zero-only TP4 accounting from understating byte costs by
up to roughly four times. Legacy fake-engine tests may still expose a single
`memory_snapshot()`; the real `LLMEngine` path preferentially uses the
all-rank transport.

The performance/cache authority no longer defines workloads by token counts

```text

token ID domain:

```

Every workload binds exact:

```text
shared_prefix_token_ids
source_suffix_token_ids
continuations[*].suffix_token_ids
continuations[*].prefix_overrides
continuations[*].invalidation
token_seed
spec
```

All continuation suffixes within a workload are distinct. W4 binds:

```text
continuation 0:
  token_mismatch at prefix index 512 with explicit replacement token
continuation 1:
  stale_block_generation
continuation 2:
  cache_clear
```

The worker passes this exact payload to the future real Engine adapter. The
independent verifier rejects a re-signed one-token mutation of
`workload_manifest.json`.

A real bug was found and fixed while adding this authority: the worker
previously defaulted to the SHA of canonical in-memory JSON bytes, while the
verifier compared the SHA of the on-disk canonical JSON file including its
newline. Those hashes differ. The worker now uses the same canonical JSON-file
hash domain as the verifier.

### Benchmark Adapter Request Boundary Hardening

The worker now validates a future real Engine adapter response before writing
any request row or logits file:

```text
validate_benchmark_requests(
  workload=...,
  policy=...,
  requests=...,
)
```

Required invariants:

```text
request count:
  exactly WORKLOAD_SPECS[workload].continuations
request IDs:
  non-empty, unique strings
restored_hybrid_state:
  exact bool, never truthiness coercion
prompt_tokens:
  shared_prefix_tokens + suffix_tokens
reused_kv_tokens:
  shared_prefix_tokens only for exact_restore W1/W2/W3, otherwise 0
executed_prefill_tokens:
  suffix_tokens only for exact_restore W1/W2/W3,
  otherwise full prompt_tokens
generated_tokens:
  exact frozen value
output_token_ids:
  exact generated length, non-negative integer IDs
decode_step_ns:
  exact generated_tokens - 1 length, non-negative integers
ttft_ns/e2e_ns:
  non-negative integers and e2e_ns >= ttft_ns
```

This fixed a real producer-boundary weakness: the previous row builder used
`bool(request["restored_hybrid_state"])`, so the string `"false"` would have
been recorded as a restore hit. Wrong prefill accounting and wrong output
length could also reach disk before the independent verifier rejected the
run.

The independent verifier now separately reconstructs the same accounting
from the immutable contract without importing the worker validator. Re-signed
tamper tests cover:

```text
prompt token count mutation
executed prefill mutation
generated/output/decode shape mutation
```

row. Every scenario now owns a fresh Engine/TP4 process group and must finish
cleanup before its row can be returned.


The seed fixture occurs before `begin_observation`; publication needed only to
prepare a restore/miss case cannot contaminate the authoritative
`publication_commits`, hit/miss, scheduler-step, or ModelRunner-call counters.

```text
session = backend_factory(

session.execute_action(
  action=<ordered action>,
  scenario=<name>,

) -> structured evidence dict
session.close()
```

The audited runtime:

- executes every action in exact order;
- accepts only object evidence;
- rejects duplicate evidence fields;

- validates the completed row through the existing strict row validator;
- closes the scenario session on success and every exception path;
- remains standard-library-only.

### Engine ModelRunner Call Counter Semantics

Real-interface review found that
`configure_qwen35_hybrid_prefix_publication_runtime(...)` necessarily issues
multiple acknowledged ModelRunner control commands. Counting those together
with inference calls made the old `construct_and_bind: model_runner_calls=1`
value impossible and inconsistent with every generation scenario.

The contract now defines:

```text
MODEL_RUNNER_CALL_SEMANTICS =
  model execution calls issued by LLMEngine.step;
  control-plane acknowledged commands are excluded
```

Canonical counts:

```text
construct_and_bind:
  scheduler_steps = 0
  model_runner_calls = 0
  generated_tokens = 0

publish/restore/miss scenarios:
  model_runner_calls == scheduler_steps == generated_tokens
```

Control-plane execution is not ignored: rank coverage remains independently
required through `rank_inventory`, `ack_ranks`, runtime configuration
evidence, cache snapshots, rank exit codes, and cleanup evidence. This change
only separates the counter domains so a real backend can measure them
honestly.

```text
process_group_destroyed

rank_cleanup_receipts
```

group destruction, every child exit code is zero, and no child remains alive.
No-exception return alone is not cleanup evidence.

The official backend uses a persistent spawn worker process. The child binds
the first frozen physical GPU through `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` before importing
Torch/Transformers, loads the model once, and serves all five requests over a
bounded pipe. The parent requires a ready handshake, structured responses,
explicit cleanup receipt, no live worker, and exit code zero. Startup,
generation, worker-response, and cleanup failures poison the backend and
kill/join/close the worker rather than falling back in-process.

Inside the worker, loading is local-only HuggingFace with
`trust_remote_code=False`, BF16, eager attention, `inference_mode()`,
deterministic greedy decoding, and equal
`min_new_tokens/max_new_tokens`. It verifies the model-manifest hash and every
listed model-file size/SHA before loading, validates the generated prompt
prefix and completion length, and explicitly releases the model/CUDA cache.
All current tests inject fake Torch/Transformers implementations; no real GPU
or model load occurred.

### 2026-07-29 Goal Coverage Audit: Speed Versus Cache Reduction

The active objective has three separate deliverables:

1. no model-quality or accuracy regression;
2. faster inference on repeated-prefix workloads;
3. lower physical cache or memory cost.

The current prompt-to-artifact coverage is:

| Deliverable | Required real evidence | Current state |
|---|---|---|
| No accuracy regression | TP4 root-logit, cached-continuation, and constructed Engine correctness authorities, plus exact benchmark output-token/logit equality | blocked on attempt18 GPU resource gate |
| Faster inference | strict-exclusive canonical P0 recompute versus P1 exact-restore benchmark, independently verified against frozen TTFT/throughput/decode thresholds | protocol implemented; no real canonical run |
| Cache cost characterized | P1 physical/logical/deduplicated bytes, all-rank CUDA memory, KV-capacity parity, and eviction evidence | protocol implemented; no real canonical run |
| Cache physically reduced | a P2 compressed candidate compared with full-fidelity P1 under the same workload and quality rules | not implemented or authorized |

The existing exact benchmark is intentionally a speed-versus-cache-cost
authority, not a cache-reduction authority:

```text
P0:
  recompute, zero hybrid-prefix snapshot bytes
P1:
  exact full-fidelity restore, up to 2 GiB physical hybrid cache
P1 GO requirements:
  W1 TTFT ratio <= 0.85
  W2 TTFT ratio <= 0.75
  W3 throughput ratio >= 1.15
  decode ratio <= 1.02
  peak CUDA reserved ratio <= 1.10
  scheduler-visible KV capacity exactly equal
  physical cache bytes <= configured limit
  cache accounting exact
```

A P1 `GO` would prove that exact restore buys registered speed improvements
within a bounded added-cache budget. It would not prove that the engine uses
less cache than recomputation, because P0 intentionally has zero hybrid
snapshot bytes.

Closing the final “cache more economical” objective requires a later
single-candidate P2 authority. The existing contract already reserves:

```text
int4_state
token_sparse_state
low_rank_state
gist_layer_share
```

That P2 authority must retain P0 and P1, use P1 as the numerical and physical
cache reference, require candidate output/logit quality against P1, report
actual physical bytes including metadata, and require a preregistered physical
compression threshold before claiming cache savings. Logical compression or
packed-storage size alone is insufficient.

Therefore the overall objective is not complete even after a future P1
benchmark `GO`: P1 closes the exact speed/cache-cost baseline; a separately
approved and independently verified P2 run is required to close physical
cache reduction.

The cache stores 36 rank-local tensors per snapshot and performs exact,

the destination batch and writes original BF16 convolution plus FP32 recurrent
state through `Qwen35CrossLayerStateTransaction.commit()`. Any lossy
representation must therefore decode completely before the existing
transaction validates or mutates the live pool.

The selected first P2 candidate is:

```text
keep convolution state exact BF16
quantize recurrent state only
per [head, value_row, :] length-128 row
symmetric INT8 values in [-127, 127]
one FP32 scale per row
```

These are layout calculations only, not measured physical cache savings.


The reference codec provides:

```text
codec:
  qwen35_recurrent_symmetric_int8_per_row_v1
input:
  rank-three finite FP32 recurrent tensor
grouping:
  one scale per recurrent[head, value_row, :]
values:
  signed INT8 in [-127, 127], with -128 forbidden
scale:
  FP32, amax / 127, with exact 1.0 for an all-zero row
decode:
  FP32 values * scale
accounting:
  logical, payload, scale, and encoded bytes kept separate
```

The offline producer:

- performs full source-bundle, threshold, hash, symlink, regular-file, and
  closed-inventory preflight before creating output;
- preserves the exact source tensor serialization bytes in the evidence
  bundle;
- writes encoded values, scales, decoded tensors, rows, summary, commands,
  and artifact inventory;
- writes `failure.json` with exact completed tensor IDs on a mid-run failure;
- never writes a partial `summary.json` or `artifact_manifest.json`;
- binds the producer summary to both source-manifest and threshold hashes;
- redacts all runtime argv values and keeps only the executable basename;
- remains producer-only and creates no independent authority files.

The independent verifier:

- is single-use and closes both file and directory inventory;
- verifies every artifact path, size, and SHA-256;
- validates source and threshold schemas independently;
- requires the producer source/threshold provenance bindings;
- reconstructs expected rank/workload/layer tensor identities and exact row
  ordering;
- loads every source, values, scales, and decoded tensor on CPU;
- independently requires the canonical `amax / 127` scale and canonical
  rounded/clamped INT8 values, rather than accepting merely self-consistent
  altered values;
- independently decodes and requires exact equality with the saved decoded
  tensor;
- independently recomputes byte equations, zero rows, saturation, and all
  error metrics in FP64;
- independently classifies `PASS | NO_GO` from frozen thresholds and does not
  trust the producer summary classification;
- emits `independent_verification.json` plus a report with an explicit claim
  boundary.

   the same start-time ticks before signaling; this covers spawned TP worker
   processes whose own `cmdline` does not repeat the run tag while protecting
   against PID reuse;
10. converts local `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` into `SystemExit` while a launch is
   active, so the same `BaseException` cleanup path runs before the detached
   monitor exits;
11. queries the remote compute-app PID inventory after cleanup and requires
    that no still-matching run PID remains in that inventory;
12. limits the canonical `workers` command to `43200` seconds; timeout returns
    code `124`, the schema-v1 executor writes failure evidence, and the monitor

```text
w3_batched_fanout__warmup__r0__exact_restore
ValueError: in_proj_qkv token count must equal 64
```

Remote failure evidence remains under:

```text
/data00/home/sitian/sitian-workspace01/tllm/
qwen35-tp4-hybrid-prefix-benchmark-runs/
qwen35-tp4-strict-p1-canonical-20260810-r599-attempt001/
output/cases/w3_batched_fanout__warmup__r0__exact_restore/failure.json
```

The error is not a projection-weight or checkpoint problem. Exact restore
produces eight request-local suffix segments of 64 tokens. The packed linear
layer invokes linear attention separately for each 64-row segment, but each
call still sees the whole batch's eight-request `cu_seqlens_q/k`. Therefore
`_project_context_rows()` emits eight 64-row projection segments (512 rows)
for a 64-row request, and `_validate_projection()` rejects it.

The subsequent exception cleanup also reported:

```text
hybrid state tensor lease mismatch:
slot=0, current=(8, 3), expected=(0, 1)
```

Treat that lease error as a secondary exception-path symptom until the primary
projection mismatch is removed and the release path is retested.

#### Pending design approval

Several consecutive remote failures exposed the same architectural issue:
components execute per request while consulting mutable whole-batch Context.
Do not apply another isolated field slice.

Recommended design:

```text
extract one packed-stack request-local Context slicer;
use it for both full-attention and linear-attention per-request calls;
cover prefill and decode metadata rebasing;
add a RED regression reproducing the exact-restore 64-to-512 projection error;
verify exception-path hybrid-state lease release after the primary fix;
use fresh monitor and run tags for the next remote attempt.
```

Approval is pending. No further monitor was started after r598, and no code
for this design has been written yet.

port and hit `EADDRINUSE`. The remote runner now scans below the temporary
port range lower bound, with focused source tests covering the protocol.

`r603` crossed the port failure and reached case 43/70, then failed in:

```text
w3_batched_fanout__warmup__r0__exact_restore
RuntimeError: mlp shape must remain unchanged
```

The packed Qwen3.5 layer stack now installs request-local Context for full
attention, linear attention, and the complete per-request linear decoder
layer. The focused regression covers eight 64-token restored continuations
and MLP isolation. The relevant combined regression before `r605` was:

```text
98 passed, 1 warning
```

`r605` crossed both prior failures and again reached case 43/70, then failed
in the same exact-restore fanout case with:

```text
ValueError: leases must reference distinct slot ids
```

The worker later aborted after the NCCL watchdog timeout. Scoped cleanup
completed; the old root PIDs `3781323` and `3781324` are gone. Monitor `r604`
is stopped with last exit code zero.

#### Confirmed lifecycle root cause

The Scheduler releases a completed request's allocator lease immediately and
queues the corresponding rank-local tensor-pool release event. Ordinarily
that queue is delivered with the next ModelRunner `run` call.

The `w3_batched_fanout` adapter completes the source request and then invokes
eight continuation `add_request()` calls before the next `engine.step()`.
Each `add_request()` attempts hybrid-prefix restore. Before this fix, restore
acquisition did not flush the queued source release to every ModelRunner rank.
The Scheduler allocator could therefore reuse a slot while rank-local pools
still held the previous lease generation.

Evidence excluding transport corruption:

```text
eight consecutive allocator allocations were unique
Sequence pickle retained request/slot/generation
the 8 x 2112-token ModelRunner envelope survived the 1 MiB transport
the serialized payload was approximately 49,200 bytes
```

#### Implemented fix

`LLMEngine.flush_pending_hybrid_state_releases(timeout_s=...)` now:

```text
1. drains Scheduler pending release events;
2. broadcasts release_hybrid_state through the acknowledged command path;
3. waits for all ModelRunner ranks;
4. restores the exact release queue if dispatch or acknowledgement fails.
```

`_try_qwen35_hybrid_prefix_restore()` invokes that flush before acquiring a
restore ticket, using the configured restore coordinator timeout. This is a
rank-synchronized lifecycle boundary; it is not a rank-0-only release and it
does not weaken duplicate-lease validation.

The ModelRunner duplicate-slot fail-fast remains in place and reports rank
plus every `(request_id, slot_id, generation)` tuple.

The makespan result is not a stable performance win. The median of the five
paired speedup ratios is `0.98695x`, which makes exact restore approximately
1.3 percent slower by that statistic. The ratio of the two policy medians is
`5.585320 / 5.557554 = 1.00500x`, which makes exact restore approximately
0.5 percent faster. The direction change between these valid summaries shows
that the approximately one-percent end-to-end difference is smaller than
run-to-run decode/makespan variation.

Exact-restore median timing detail for one four-continuation case:

```text
restore total:                        43.620390 ms
restore total per request:            10.905097 ms
restore prepare:                      26.119403 ms
restore validate:                      5.460653 ms
restore commit:                        5.288011 ms
restore rollback:                      0
source release flush:                  8.587997 ms
```

`restore_prepare` accounts for about `59.879%` of `restore_total`, but its
rank-local versus acknowledgement/transport split is not measured. Even if
all of the complete `43.620390 ms` restore interval were charged to
communication/synchronization, it would still be less than one percent of the
approximately `5.56 s` exact-restore makespan. It therefore cannot explain
the missing end-to-end speedup.

All four continuation output token-ID sequences matched between recompute and
exact restore in every one of the five measured repetitions. This profile
therefore supports the timing comparison without introducing a token-output
behavior difference.

#### Conclusion and next experiment

For this workload, exact restore eliminates `15,360 / 15,616` executed
prefill tokens and improves median TTFT by about `33.8 ms`, but decode takes
about `4.71 s` and approximately `84.7%` of makespan. Decode variation is
larger than the restore overhead and the observed TTFT saving, so it dilutes
the prefill reduction in end-to-end time.

The next useful performance experiment is not deeper restore profiling by
default. Use one or both of:

```text
1. the same long prefix with a much shorter generated output, to expose TTFT
   and prefill savings without a multi-second decode tail;
2. a continuous online session with repeated continuations, to amortize
   setup and measure sustained reuse behavior.
```

Only instrument below `restore_prepare` if optimizing the remaining roughly
`26 ms` prepare interval is itself the goal; it is not the dominant
end-to-end bottleneck in the current `w2_long_reuse` workload.

regression. Across repetitions, exact restore often had slightly slower
steady-state decode steps, and one repetition had a materially slower decode
interval. TP communication, CUDA kernels, and synchronization waits were not
instrumented, so this profile does not locate the decode-internal cause.

#### Short-output conclusion

The eight-token experiment falsifies the simple hypothesis that a stable
end-to-end reuse win was merely hidden by a 64-token decode tail. Prefix reuse
is functionally effective and removes 98.36 percent of executed prefill
tokens, but under this four-continuation shared-GPU setup it does not reduce
TTFT or makespan reliably. The next performance work should therefore avoid
deeper restore subdivision by default and instead isolate:

```text
1. first decode step versus steady-state per-token latency;
2. TP collective time and synchronization waiting;
3. CUDA kernel timelines for recompute versus exact restore;
4. whether restored-state ownership/layout changes the subsequent decode path.
```

## 2026-08-12 generic speculative KV transaction contract

The first model-independent runtime slice for generic MTP/speculative
decoding is implemented in:

```text
tinyvllm/engine/block_manager.py
tools/test_speculative_kv_transaction.py
```

Design and execution plan:

```text
docs/superpowers/specs/
  2026-08-12-generic-speculative-kv-transaction-design.md
docs/superpowers/plans/
  2026-08-12-generic-speculative-kv-transaction.md
```

New public contract:

```text
SpeculativeKVTransaction
BlockManager.begin_speculative_kv_transaction()
BlockManager.mark_speculative_kv_materialized()
BlockManager.commit_speculative_kv_transaction()
BlockManager.rollback_speculative_kv_transaction()
```

State machine:

```text
reserved -> materialized -> committed
reserved -> rolled_back
materialized -> rolled_back
```

The transaction records sequence ownership, the original token/block-table
snapshot, private reserved block IDs and generations, proposal size, and
explicit materialized appended-KV count. Commit validates the owner,
snapshot, accepted/materialized bounds, live ownership, unpublished private
blocks, and generations before mutating `Sequence`. It attaches only blocks
needed by accepted materialized KV, publishes only full materialized blocks,
and releases the rejected suffix. Rollback is exactly once and remains
available after same-owner sequence drift.

One additional RED test found and closed a malformed-ownership hole:
`original_block_table` and `reserved_block_ids` must be unique and disjoint,
otherwise a forged transaction could attach the same block twice.

```text
  tools/test_chunked_prefill.py
chunked prefill tests passed

Python 3.9 py_compile:  PASS
Python 3.12 py_compile: PASS
git diff --check:       PASS
staged diff:            empty
```

Validation limitation:

```text
tools/test_model_runner_spec_verify.py
```

is currently blocked during source-loader collection because its
dependency-light harness does not install the existing
`tinyvllm.engine.decode_internal_profiler` module imported by
`model_runner.py`. This was not counted as a pass or a transaction failure.

This phase proves only a CPU/model-independent ownership contract. It does
not prove scheduler integration, real MTP, GPU/TP behavior, long-context
behavior, exact greedy model parity, TPOT, TTFT, throughput, memory, KV H2D
bytes, or acceptance improvement. No simulated H2D result is used.

Next gate:

1. migrate native `verify_and_commit_block()` from bare reserved block IDs to
   `SpeculativeKVTransaction`;
2. preserve direct accepted-KV commit and zero rematerialization;
3. move source-agnostic verify/accept/commit orchestration from the profiler
   into `tinyvllm/speculative/`;
4. then integrate batched scheduler ownership before adding MTP adapters or
   KV-offload residency coordination.

## 2026-08-12 native verifier transaction migration

The first next gate above is complete. Native
`verify_and_commit_block()` now uses:

```text
begin_speculative_kv_transaction
-> target first decode
-> native multi-token tail forward
-> mark_speculative_kv_materialized(query_len)
-> acceptance/EOS/budget truncation
-> commit_speculative_kv_transaction
```

Any native failure before successful commit calls
`rollback_speculative_kv_transaction`. Tail-forward failure rolls back from
`reserved`; metadata-commit failure rolls back from `materialized`. Cleanup
failure details are appended to the original phase-labelled native verifier
error.

`verifier_mode="legacy_rematerialize"` remains on:

```text
reserve_append_blocks
-> rematerialize_accepted_kv
-> commit_accepted_tokens
```

This isolation is intentional. The legacy path still covers existing
offload/profiler experiments and was not silently moved onto native
materialization semantics.

The transaction's `N - 1` capacity rule also removes an old boundary
over-reservation. For sequence length `3`, block size `4`, and a two-token
proposal, the one native tail KV entry fits in the existing block, so no
extra block is reserved. Failure rollback still executes exactly once with
an empty reservation.

### Loaded-gate workload correction

The first worker configuration used the default:

```text
chunked_prefill_decode_first=True
```

That caused each long request to finish prefill and decode before the next
request, so nominal batch 4 was effectively serialized and produced zero H2D.
The gate now explicitly uses:

```text
chunked_prefill_decode_first=False
chunked_prefill_mixed_batch=False
max_num_prefill_tokens_per_step=1024
```

This fills all long prompts before decode and creates a real concurrent
batch-4 fixed-budget geometry.

### Persistent remote runner hardening

The remote runner no longer keeps the eight-cell campaign attached to one
long SSH command. It now:

```text
publishes campaign.sh through campaign.sh.tmp + atomic mv
starts the campaign with nohup
writes campaign.pid
writes RUNNING/COMPLETE/FAILED to campaign.status
writes the terminal return code to campaign.exit_code
polls through short SSH commands
detects a dead RUNNING pid and records exit code 125
fails closed on a stale RUNNING pid during reattachment instead of silently
  relaunching over partial failure evidence
always attempts artifact download and local verification
can reattach without relaunching when rerun with the same RUN_TAG
```

If polling loses SSH, the local runner exits after an attempted download and
prints the exact `RUN_TAG`; the remote `nohup` process is expected to continue.
After authentication is restored, rerun with that same `RUN_TAG` to observe
the existing PID/terminal status and recover the artifact.

## 2026-08-12 generic draft adapter and batch runtime core

The next dependency-light layer above the single-sequence runtime is complete:

```text
tinyvllm/speculative/adapter.py
tinyvllm/speculative/batch_runtime.py
tinyvllm/speculative/__init__.py
```

Design and implementation plan:

```text
docs/superpowers/specs/
  2026-08-12-generic-draft-adapter-batch-runtime-design.md
docs/superpowers/plans/
  2026-08-12-generic-draft-adapter-batch-runtime.md
```

The adapter contract exposes:

```text
DraftCapabilities
DraftContext
DraftProposal
DraftAdapter
validate_draft_adapter_batch()
```

It validates exact unique sequence coverage, immutable token-history
snapshots, capability-required hidden/logit payloads, proposal bounds,
integer token IDs, source identity, and finite non-negative timing. Adapter
result order is not trusted; validated proposals are returned in input
sequence order.

`remaining_output_tokens` is advisory adapter input. It is not a proposal
hard limit because the runtime remains authoritative for output-budget
truncation.

The batch runtime exposes:

```text
FirstTargetResult
TailBatchItem
TailBatchResult
NativeSpeculativeSequenceResult
NativeSpeculativeBatchResult
NativeSpeculativeBatchError
execute_native_speculative_batch()
```

For a selected batch it:

1. executes exactly one first-target callback;
2. executes one adapter proposal batch;
3. begins one speculative transaction for each non-empty proposal;
4. executes at most one tail callback for all `query_len > 0` rows;
5. validates every tail row before materializing any transaction;
6. marks exact per-row materialized KV counts;
7. computes zero/one/partial/full greedy acceptance, EOS, and output-budget
   truncation independently;
8. commits accepted prefixes in stable input order;
9. rolls back every uncommitted transaction after any failure;
10. reports committed IDs, successful rollbacks, and rollback failures if a
    later commit fails.

K=0 creates no transaction. K=1 creates a transaction, skips the tail batch,
and marks zero appended KV. Accepted KV is committed through
`commit_speculative_kv_transaction()`; the core contains no token replay,
accepted-KV copy, or rematerialization path.

## 2026-08-12 concrete n-gram and SAM runtime adapters

Concrete proposal sources now implement the generic adapter protocol:

```text
tinyvllm/speculative/ngram_adapter.py
```

Design and completed implementation plan:

```text
docs/superpowers/specs/
  2026-08-12-ngram-sam-runtime-adapters-design.md
docs/superpowers/plans/
  2026-08-12-ngram-sam-runtime-adapters.md
```

`NGramDraftAdapter` is stateless. It wraps
`propose_ngram_draft()`, preserves batch input order and IDs, caps proposals
by adapter/context limits, treats `remaining_output_tokens` as advisory, and
returns explicit match/bypass metadata.

`SAMDraftAdapter` owns:

```text
sequence_id -> SuffixAutomatonDraftIndex
```

Its lifecycle is explicit:

```text
register_sequence()
propose_batch()
synchronize_verified_history()
release_sequence()
```

Proposal requires an exact match between the context token snapshot and the
indexed target-verified history. Proposal is read-only. Synchronization
validates the complete history before mutation, appends only the new verified
suffix, and rejects truncation or prefix rewrite without changing the index.
Rejected draft tokens never enter the index. Fixed-K and match-aware policies
both obey the generic adapter/context maximums.

The public package now exports:

```text
NGramDraftAdapter
SAMDraftAdapter
```

Public contracts:

```text
EngineSpeculativePartition
EngineSpeculativeCommitRow
build_engine_speculative_partition()
build_engine_speculative_commit_rows()
```

`build_engine_speculative_partition()` delegates generation, sequence-order,
token-count, completion-count, and output-budget stale checks to the immutable
selection validator. It preserves selected and suppressed batch order and
requires disjoint exact coverage of scheduled IDs.

`build_engine_speculative_commit_rows()` validates exact ordered runtime IDs,
integer target/proposal tokens, bounded greedy acceptance, and accepted draft
prefixes. It produces final tokens without mutating `Sequence`:

```text
empty proposal:
  first target
zero acceptance:
  first target
partial acceptance:
  accepted draft prefix + mismatch target
full acceptance:
  accepted draft prefix only
accepted EOS or exhausted output budget:
  suppress mismatch target
```

Only `accepted_draft_tokens` correspond to already committed speculative KV.
The fallback target token remains an ordinary next-input token and is not
claimed as transaction-committed KV.

`LLMEngine.step()` now consumes
`scheduler.last_speculative_selection` immediately after parsing the legacy
three/four-element scheduler tuple. Default-disabled selection preserves the
ordinary ModelRunner path. Any selected row raises:

```text

```

The guard runs before hybrid-state release draining or
`model_runner.call("run", ...)`, so configured speculation cannot silently
fall back while observations claim selected execution.

## 2026-08-12 greedy KV-only ModelRunner first-target batch

The production-shaped callback pair is now:

```text
ModelRunner.run_spec_first_target_batch()
ModelRunner.run_spec_verify_batch()
```

`run_spec_first_target_batch()` accepts a non-empty tuple of unique sequences,
requires `temperature == 0`, calls `prepare_decode()` once, executes one target
`run_model(..., execution_mode="decode")`, and returns ordered
`FirstTargetResult` rows on rank zero. It can expose per-row hidden states and
logits for adapters that declare those capabilities. Worker ranks execute the
same forward and return `None`.

Both first-target and tail paths now fail closed when
`hybrid_state_runtime_bridge` is active:

```text
speculative verification requires transactional non-KV state
```

This is a correctness boundary, not a model-name branch. The current
transaction owns KV blocks only; recurrent or convolution state cannot be
allowed to retain rejected speculative suffix mutations.

The first-target method also rejects nonzero temperature because the current
runtime implements greedy prefix acceptance, not stochastic speculative
rejection sampling. Scheduler selection still needs an earlier non-greedy
suppression rule before engine wiring.

## 2026-08-12 greedy speculative selection temperature snapshot

Scheduler selection now distinguishes "produce an output token" from "greedy
sampling." `do_sample=True` is no longer sufficient for speculative
selection.

Every immutable `SpeculativeSelectionRow` now carries:

```text
temperature_snapshot: float
```

The builder validates a finite numeric temperature and applies this
suppression precedence:

```text
disabled
prefill
not_sampling
non_greedy
insufficient_output_budget
selected
```

Rows with `temperature != 0.0` are published as suppressed with
`suppression_reason="non_greedy"` and zero proposal budget.

Engine-side record validation compares the live sequence temperature with the
snapshot and rejects stale mutation. It also rejects a malformed record that
marks a non-greedy row selected even when its snapshot matches.

The ModelRunner greedy-temperature check remains as defense in depth.

## 2026-08-12 speculative ModelRunner callback bridge

The engine now has a dependency-light adapter between generic batch runtime
callbacks and all-rank `ModelRunner.call()`:

```text
tinyvllm/engine/speculative_model_runner.py
```

Public contracts:

```text
FixedQTailBatch
build_fixed_q_tail_batches()
run_model_runner_first_targets()
run_model_runner_tail_batch()
```

`run_model_runner_first_targets()` performs exactly one:

```text
ModelRunner.call(
  "run_spec_first_target_batch",
  seqs,
  requires_target_hidden,
  requires_target_logits,
)
```

It validates exact unique result IDs and restores input sequence order.
`run_spec_first_target_batch()` now accepts the two capability flags as
positional-or-keyword arguments because the shared-memory command transport
currently carries positional arguments only.

`run_model_runner_tail_batch()` groups rows by exact positive query length,
orders groups by the first occurrence of each Q, preserves row order within
each group, and executes one `run_spec_verify_batch` RPC per distinct Q. It
validates each `SpecVerifyBatchResultRow` group and merges
`TailBatchResult` rows back to original callback order.

Example:

```text
input:
  seq8/Q2, seq4/Q1, seq2/Q2, seq9/Q3
physical verifier RPCs:
  Q2=(seq8,seq2), Q1=(seq4), Q3=(seq9)
merged result:
  seq8, seq4, seq2, seq9
```

No padding or per-sequence target forward is used. If a later fixed-Q group
fails, the generic batch runtime remains responsible for rolling back every
active transaction, including KV written by earlier groups.

## 2026-08-12 prepared speculative runtime and atomic KV commit

Generic batch execution has been split into explicit phases:

```text
prepare_native_speculative_batch()
commit_prepared_native_speculative_batch()
rollback_prepared_native_speculative_batch()
```

Prepare performs:

- one first-target callback for the selected batch;
- proposal generation;
- per-sequence private KV reservation;
- fixed-Q tail verification;
- KV materialization accounting;
- greedy acceptance and EOS/output-budget truncation.

Prepare does **not**:

- append tokens;
- extend live sequence block tables;
- publish prefix hashes;
- release rejected suffix blocks.

BlockManager now exposes:

```text
prepare_speculative_kv_commit()
commit_speculative_kv_commit_batch()
```

The planner computes exact committed/unused block IDs and prefix-cache
publications from `original_token_ids + accepted_tokens` without mutation.
The batch commit:

- validates every plan before mutation;
- extends block ownership without appending tokens;
- publishes precomputed full-block hashes;
- releases unused reservations;
- snapshots and restores allocator ownership, blocks, hash indexes, sequence
  block tables, and transaction states on any failure.

The legacy `execute_native_speculative_batch()` remains available for profiler
callers. It now runs:

```text
prepare -> atomic token-free KV commit -> append accepted tokens
```

Therefore a KV commit-batch failure no longer leaves an earlier sequence
partially committed.

## 2026-08-12 engine speculative Scheduler wiring completed

Production `LLMEngine.step()` now executes the generic speculative selection
record instead of unconditionally rejecting selected rows:

- no installed runtime and poisoned runtime remain fail-closed before
  ModelRunner work;
- suppressed rows execute through the ordinary `run` path with original row
  metadata and carry pending hybrid-state releases exactly once;
- selected rows prepare through one first-target batch callback and one tail
  callback per distinct fixed query length;
- selected and suppressed output rows merge in original Scheduler order;
- Scheduler preparation occurs before KV publication;
- KV plans commit as one batch, followed by one prepared Scheduler metadata
  commit;
- KV commit failure rolls back all active reservations without publishing
  sequence tokens;
- Scheduler commit failure restores its snapshot, returns committed
  transaction objects to `materialized`, and rolls back selected reservations;
- optional draft lifecycle histories synchronize from committed target
  histories and release finished rows only after synchronization;
- lifecycle failure leaves target state committed, poisons the runtime, and
  blocks later selected execution before ModelRunner callbacks.

```text
tinyvllm/engine/block_manager.py

tools/test_speculative_tp1_parity_gate.py
```

Allocator and residency identity is `(logical_block_id, generation)`.
Ordinary MVP-0 decode binds allocator generations before physical mapping.
Speculative tail verification uses one engine-owned ticket across all
distinct fixed-Q groups without padding. Each group materializes a disjoint
ticket subset; precommit requires the complete ticket.

Publication order:

```text
residency prepare
verifier forward(s)
residency precommit
allocator commit
Scheduler commit
residency seal
optional lifecycle synchronization
```

Failure boundaries:

- before allocator publication: rollback residency, then allocator
  reservations;
- residency rollback failure: poison runtime and stop later selected work;
- Scheduler commit failure: restore Scheduler snapshot, then roll back
  residency and native reservations;
- seal failure: keep committed target tokens and ownership, poison runtime,
  and do not attempt post-publication rollback.

Two loaded-model bring-up bugs were fixed and regression-tested:

1. first-target decode incorrectly reused the tail verifier's prepared-ticket
   requirement even though the ticket is created only after proposals and
   reservations exist;
2. fixed-Q verifier groups were rejected because the participant required
   every verifier RPC to contain the whole ticket instead of a disjoint
   sequence subset.


`KVOffloadMVP0.evict_clean_resident_blocks()` now atomically validates a
tuple of `(logical_block, generation)` identities, requires resident clean
CPU-valid blocks with no pending H2D, removes only GPU mapping/event state,
preserves CPU backing and generation, and increments `evictions` plus
`evict_clean`.

The loaded-model gate uses:

```text
prompt tokens:
  254
live length after prefill:
  255
max_tokens:
  4
fixture proposal:
  3 baseline-derived greedy tokens
```

Important correction: speculative reservation covers
`proposal_count - 1` materialized tail tokens. The original one-token fixture
could not reserve a block at length 255 and also violated the generic
selection minimum. The corrected three-token fixture materializes positions
255 and 256, forcing a second block without changing generic runtime behavior.
The accept fixture proposes the exact baseline suffix; the reject fixture
changes its first token. Both fail closed if the live first target token
differs from the baseline-derived fixture.

The real gate found three loader defects that were fixed with TDD:

1. `ModelRunner` registration attempted to build private MTP parameters
   directly on CUDA even though the shared component factory only supports
   `meta` or `cpu`.

   Final order:

   ```text
   CPU module construction
   -> read all 15 CPU checkpoint tensors
   -> transactional checkpoint binding
   -> move the MTP module to the target embedding device
   -> verify shared embedding/lm_head object identity
   -> build proposal executor
   ```

2. `bind_qwen35_mtp_checkpoint()` required every destination to expose a
   custom `weight_loader`. Ordinary RMSNorm-like parameters now use the same
   default `destination.data.copy_(source)` behavior as the standard model
   loader. Packed destinations still require a callable custom loader.

3. The checkpoint plan mislabeled the already separate q/k/v projection
   parameters as packed QKV slots. The full-attention builder actually uses
   `ReplicatedHeadPairedColumnParallelLinear` for q and
   `ReplicatedKVHeadParallelLinear` for k/v; all inherit the ordinary
   two-argument `ReplicatedLinear.weight_loader`. Only gate/up remain packed
   into `gate_up_proj` with slots 0 and 1.

## Qwen3.5 MTP physical-KV transaction follow-up

The transaction work from the preceding implementation order is now complete.
The Qwen3.5-local proposal store owns real device-resident K/V tensors with
block size one. The loaded MTP attention backend writes directly into those
tensors through exact bootstrap-prefill and proposal-decode contexts.

Transaction behavior:

```text
accepted proposal K/V:
  committed in the original physical slots
  slot IDs, data pointers, and values remain unchanged
  no accepted-KV replay, copy, or rematerialization

rejected proposal suffix:
  ownership released during rollback/finalize
  released K/V rows zeroed before slot reuse

cached continuation:
  committed slots plus the current staged prefix are visible to each step
  two identical post-rollback continuations produce equal token outputs
  committed K/V remains unchanged across continuation rollbacks
```

## 2026-08-13 Native-MTP target-forward evidence hardening

The TP1/4K native-MTP authority no longer relies only on callback counters or
on the ordinary `ModelRunner.run` replay counter. The worker now records the
actual target-forward RPC inventory for both native speculative stages:

```text
run_spec_first_target_and_proposal_batch
  -> runtime.first_target_target_forwards

run_spec_verify_batch
  -> runtime.verify_target_forwards
```

The authority validator requires:

```text
baseline:
  first_target_target_forwards == 0
  verify_target_forwards == 0

native_mtp:
  first_target_target_forwards == first_target_callbacks
  verify_target_forwards == verify_callbacks
  accepted_prefix_target_replays == 0
```

This closes the previous evidence gap where a hidden duplicate first-target
or verifier RPC could avoid the ordinary non-prefill `ModelRunner.run`
counter. A fake Engine that performs one extra
`run_spec_verify_batch` call is now rejected with a forward/callback
mismatch.

TDD and regression evidence:

```text

  mutated authority forward counts were not rejected
  an extra verifier target forward was not rejected

    tools/test_engine_speculative_runtime.py
    200 passed in 0.96s

  static validation:

    remote runner bash syntax PASS
    scoped git diff check PASS
```

The independent verifier calls the same `validate_result()` path, so these
fields are part of normalized authority semantics and result-digest
verification rather than informational-only logging.

The complete related suite is now `208 passed in 4.45s`, with Python

The exact remote source-bundle command was also replayed into an isolated
temporary directory. With only the extracted bundle on `PYTHONPATH`:

```text
qwen35_native_mtp_tp1_4k_engine_gate.py --help:
  PASS

  PASS

DEFAULT_SOURCE_FILES:
  106 / 106 present and hashed

result:
  ISOLATED_FULL_SOURCE_BUNDLE_OK
```

The authority source manifest previously listed only 10 selected files even
though the remote tar executes the complete `tinyvllm` package. It now
deterministically includes every `tinyvllm/**/*.py` file plus the gate,
worker, and independent verifier. This binds scheduler, block-manager,
sequence, model, layer, KV, and runtime changes into the authority digest
instead of leaving them outside independent verification.

The independent verifier additionally requires the manifest key set to equal
`DEFAULT_SOURCE_FILES` exactly. A deliberately reduced manifest containing
only `engine.py` previously returned `PASS`; the new RED/GREEN regression
requires it to return:

```text
classification:
  FAIL

failure:
  source file inventory mismatch
```

This prevents an authority producer from evading full source binding by
publishing a valid digest over a selectively reduced file inventory.

`run_campaign()` now takes the complete source hash snapshot before any
worker process starts. After all four cells and checkpoint identity reads,
it hashes the same inventory again and requires exact mapping equality.
The result and manifest use the pre-execution snapshot digest.

A RED/GREEN campaign test mutates one bound source file after the first fake
worker cell. Before the fix, the campaign incorrectly published an authority
using the post-mutation digest. It is now rejected with:

```text
source changed during campaign
```

This binds the authority to the code present before execution and rejects
mid-campaign source drift instead of silently attesting to code that was not
used by every cell.

The independent verifier now also recomputes the aggregate source-tree hash
directly from the 106 manifest digest entries even when no `source_root` is
provided. A valid-length per-file digest was deliberately changed while the
result tree digest remained unchanged. Before the fix, offline verification
returned `PASS`; it now returns:

```text
classification:
  FAIL

failure:
  source tree digest mismatch
```

When `source_root` is supplied, the verifier additionally checks every file
content against its manifest digest. Therefore offline verification checks
manifest internal consistency, while source-backed verification checks both
internal consistency and actual file contents.

The verifier now also requires:

```text
source_manifest.schema_version:
  exactly the frozen native-MTP authority schema

source_manifest.artifacts:
  exactly result.json and status.json
```

Previously a changed manifest schema or an extra artifact digest was ignored
and still returned `PASS`. Both mutations now return `FAIL`. This prevents
semantic drift or undeclared payloads from being hidden inside an otherwise
valid authority directory.

The verifier also requires the raw `result.json` object to equal the
canonical object returned by `validate_result()`. Previously an extra field
such as:

```text
undeclared_claim:
  production_ready
```

was silently discarded by normalization and still verified as `PASS` after
the artifact digest was updated. It is now rejected with:

```text
result is not canonical
```

This prevents undeclared claims or nested payloads from being attached to a
valid native-MTP result outside the frozen schema.

The raw source manifest is now canonical as well. Its top-level key set must
be exactly:

```text
schema_version
source_tree_sha256
target_model_manifest_sha256
mtp_checkpoint_manifest_sha256
source_files
artifacts
```

Adding `undeclared_claim=production_ready` to the manifest previously
verified as `PASS`; it now fails with
`source manifest is not canonical`.

The isolated bundle proves the runner tar inventory is locally
self-contained for CLI startup, full source hashing, and source-manifest
generation. It does not prove that the remote Python environment,
checkpoint, GPU, or production Engine campaign will pass.

## 2026-08-13 Qwen3.5 Generic Speculative TP4/16K Controlled Performance Authority

The independent Qwen3.5 second-model TP4/16K controlled performance gate is
complete and independently verified. Its campaign-level direction is
`POSITIVE`, but the claim is restricted to this measured 16K configuration.

During the first performance campaign, repeated ngram cells exposed a real TP
transport defect rather than a speculative cleanup defect. Transactional
side-state phases (`prepare -> select -> apply -> seal`) had used the ordinary
TP `ModelRunner.call` path, whose shared command slot and Event are
fire-and-forget. Back-to-back phases could overwrite or coalesce before every
worker rank consumed them, leaving an active transaction and eventually
triggering the NCCL watchdog. Side-state callbacks now use an explicit ordered
dispatcher backed by acknowledged all-rank RPC; every phase must complete on
all ranks before the next phase starts.

The retained first campaign:

```text
artifacts/qwen35_generic_speculative_tp4_16k_performance/
opaque-eeda7de6aa3b0e1728f2245f/
```

when unrelated workloads occupied GPUs 2 and 3 during `baseline:b4`. Only the
owned campaign process tree was terminated. The failed run remains preserved
with exit status 143 and is not an authority.

## 2026-08-13 Qwen3.5 native MTP TP1/4K Engine transactional gate: implementation GREEN, real GPU authority blocked before launch

The next gate is the production `LLMEngine.step()` path with the real Qwen3.5
native MTP proposal executor, transactional proposal KV, and finished-sequence
cleanup. The runtime change closes the missing proposal-executor lifecycle
edge:

```text
proposal finalize commit
-> side-state seal
-> residency seal when present
-> finished proposal sequence release
-> Engine return
```

The release path is source-neutral and is routed through
`ModelRunnerProposalExecutorRegistry.release_sequence(...)`,
`release_model_runner_proposal_sequence(...)`, and the ModelRunner
`release_speculative_proposal_sequence` command. Host adapters and
non-lifecycle ModelRunner executors do not receive this callback. A release
failure poisons the speculative runtime and propagates the exception rather
than returning a partially cleaned result.

Focused and broad local evidence:

```text

native MTP TP1/4K authority contract:

  complete file after replay-observation hardening:
                          54 passed

Python compilation:
  PASS

runner bash syntax:
  PASS

scoped git diff --check:
  PASS
```

The initial authority worker incorrectly initialized
`accepted_prefix_target_replays` to zero without an observation producer. That
would have made the no-replay requirement a self-assertion. The worker now
records ordinary non-prefill `ModelRunner.run` calls per `engine.step()` and
counts them as accepted-prefix replays only when the same step reports accepted
draft tokens. A fake Engine regression injects one such replay and requires the
worker/gate to reject the cell with
`accepted-prefix target replay count must be zero`.

The TP4 correctness campaign exposed a real FlashAttention boundary:
single-token Proposal-KV pages cannot be passed as paged blocks because the
kernel requires a page size divisible by 256. Ordinary FP decode now gathers
incompatible small pages into a dense temporary read view while preserving
single-token ownership and transactional semantics. Focused attention tests
pass locally and remotely (`6 passed`), and remote blockwise planning passes
(`35 passed`).

## Real KV Movement Provenance Audit

The authoritative artifacts currently cited for generic speculative
performance and native target-KV offload were checked directly:

```text
artifacts/speculative_runtime_performance/20260812T085852Z/result.json
artifacts/qwen35_generic_speculative_tp4_16k_performance/opaque-c9807d19e6402acc22d4a615/artifacts/authority/result.json
artifacts/qwen35_native_mtp_tp4_16k_target_kv_offload/lifecycle-release-fix-20260814-2/artifacts/authority/result.json
```

None contains `simulated_upload_*`, `simulate_kv_upload_mb`, or another
simulation field. Movement is collected as four-rank before/after deltas from
`LLMEngine.kv_offload_summaries()`, which calls
`ModelRunner.kv_offload_summary()` and returns `KVOffloadMVP0.summary()`.
`KVOffloadMVP0` increments the H2D and D2H copy/byte counters in its actual
KV-cache/backing-store copy enqueue paths.

The generic TP4/16K gate validates all four rank rows, recomputes totals, and
requires positive H2D and D2H copies and bytes for both batch-4 policies. The
native TP4/16K target-KV gate independently requires positive native batch-4
target-KV H2D and D2H copies and bytes.

Native TP4/16K batch-4 per-rank authority deltas:

```text

native_mtp: h2d_copies=6762  h2d_bytes=42542825472
            d2h_copies=273   d2h_bytes=1717567488
```

Each row is repeated consistently for ranks 0-3. Native batch 1 has zero H2D
and is not claimed as bidirectional; the positive-movement gate applies to
batch 4.
